The output of a standard Bottleneck has four times as many channels as its middle representation: That is why PyTorch sets expansion = 4. The final stage of ResNet-50 outputs 2048 channels, while ResNet-18 ends with 512. 7. Building a complete ResNet from blocks A standard ImageNet ResNet can be read as: The main differences between variants are the block type and the number of repetitions per stage: Model Block Blocks in four stages Intuition for layer count Approx. parameters ResNet-18 BasicBlock 2, 2, 2, 2 8×2 + stem + FC 11.7 M ResNet-34 BasicBlock 3, 4, 6, 3 16×2 + stem + FC 21.8 M ResNet-50 Bottleneck 3, 4, 6, 3 16×3 + stem + FC 25.6 M ResNet-101 Bottleneck 3, 4, 23, 3 a much deeper middle stage 44.5 M ResNet-152 Bottleneck 3, 8, 36, 3 an even deeper third stage 60.2 M Layer counting normally includes weighted convolutional layers and the final fully connected layer, but excludes BN, ReLU, pooling and element-wise additions. A BasicBlock therefore contributes two “layers” even though its computation graph contains more operations. Why do ResNet-50 and ResNet-34 have the same number of blocks but different names? Both use [3, 4, 6, 3], or 16 blocks in total: 8. ResNet v1 and v2: the position of ReLU matters Original ResNet v1: The later paper Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks proposed pre-activation ResNet v2: V2 moves BN and ReLU before each convolution and applies no immediate activation after addition. Across many blocks, the shortcut backbone is therefore closer to a pure identity mapping, giving information and gradients a more direct route. Do not confuse v1/v2 with BasicBlock/Bottleneck: v1/v2 describe the ordering of operations; BasicBlock/Bottleneck describe the convolutional structure of the main branch. 9. Read a PyTorch BasicBlock step by step Five common questions about the code 1. Why does the convolution use bias=False? The following BatchNorm already has a learnable offset beta, and BN’s centring operation cancels the convolutional bias. Keeping both is usually redundant. 2. Why does the first convolution use stride, while the second always uses 1? Each stage only needs to downsample once. The first layer aligns the size, then the remaining computation runs on the smaller feature map. 3. Why out + identity rather than concatenation? The residual formula uses element-wise addition, which does not increase the channel count. 4. Why avoid out += identity? An in-place operation can overwrite an intermediate value still needed by autograd. Ordinary addition is safer. 5. What is nn.Identity() for? It returns its input unchanged, so forward does not need two different code paths. Verify the shapes with a small experiment: 10. Seven mistakes beginners often make Mistake 1: treating the residual as the classification error $F(x)=H(x)-x$ is an internal feature difference. The training loss compares the final prediction with the target label. They are not the same thing. Mistake 2: assuming the shortcut always performs no computation When the shape is unchanged the shortcut is Identity; when the shape changes it commonly contains a 1×1 convolution and BN. Mistake 3: replacing addition with channel concatenation torch.cat([out, identity], dim=1) doubles the channels. That resembles a DenseNet or U-Net connection, not a standard ResNet shortcut. Mistake 4: adding branches with incompatible shapes If you see an error such as “The size of tensor a must match…”, print the shapes of both branches and check the channel count, stride and padding. Mistake 5: thinking ResNet only solves vanishing gradients It does improve gradient flow, but the original paper directly targeted the optimisation degradation of deep plain networks. BN and sensible initialisation had already reduced basic exploding/vanishing-gradient problems; residual structure made the deeper optimisation landscape easier still. Mistake 6: assuming deeper is always better for your task Deeper networks are slower, use more memory and depend more strongly on data volume and training strategy. On a small dataset, a pretrained ResNet-18/34 can be more reliable than training ResNet-101 from scratch. Mistake 7: forgetting the input channel count ImageNet-pretrained models normally expect three RGB channels. For grayscale medical images, either repeat the image across three channels or modify the first convolution and decide how to transfer its pretrained weights. 11. Using ResNet in medical-image segmentation A U-Net encoder repeatedly downsamples and extracts multi-scale features, so its ordinary convolutional encoder is often replaced with a pretrained ResNet: This commonly provides two benefits: ImageNet pretraining supplies stable low-level edge and texture features, which are valuable when medical labels are scarce. Residual connections keep a deeper encoder reasonably easy to train. Watch the output stride. The deepest feature map of a classification ResNet is normally only $1/32$ of the input resolution, which can erase tiny lesions. Segmentation models often remove a late downsampling step, replace it with dilated convolution, or rely on a strong decoder and high-resolution skip connections. 12. Use ResNet to understand later networks Once a residual block is separated into its main branch, shortcut and fusion operation, many later models become easier to read: Work What changed? One-sentence interpretation DenseNet fusion replace addition with channel concatenation and preserve every older feature SENet end of main branch learn an importance weight for each channel before addition Res2Net inside main branch create hierarchical multi-scale residuals inside one block ResNeXt inside main branch use parallel grouped transformations to increase cardinality ResNet v2 operation order pre-activation keeps the identity shortcut cleaner 13. Three self-check questions Answer each one before expanding it. 1. If the ideal behaviour of a residual block is to change nothingIt should learn $F(x)=0$, so $y=F(x)+x=x$. 2. The input is 64×56×56 and the main-branch output is 128×28×28. Why can they not be added directly?Element-wise addition requires identical channel, height and width dimensions. Use a 1×1 convolution with stride=2 on the shortcut to project the input to 128×28×28. 3. Why does ResNet-50 use Bottleneck rather than BasicBlock?Later stages have many channels. Bottleneck first reduces the channel count with a 1×1 convolution, runs the expensive 3×3 convolution in the narrow representation, and then expands again. This permits much greater depth at manageable parameter and compute cost. Final review checklist ResNet addresses training degradation in deep plain networks, not merely overfitting. A plain block learns $H(x)$; a residual block learns $F(x)=H(x)-x$ and outputs $F(x)+x$. When the ideal mapping is close to identity, learning $F(x)\approx0$ is easier. Shortcuts provide direct routes for forward information and backward gradients. BasicBlock uses two 3×3 convolutions in ResNet-18/34. Bottleneck uses 1×1 → 3×3 → 1×1 in ResNet-50/101/152. When the two branches have different shapes, a 1×1 projection shortcut aligns them. Residual addition is not the same operation as channel concatenation in U-Net or DenseNet. References He et al., Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition, CVPR 2016, arXiv:1512.03385 He et al., Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks, ECCV 2016, arXiv:1603.05027 Xie et al., Aggregated Residual Transformations for Deep Neural Networks, CVPR 2017, arXiv:1611.05431 PyTorch, source for torchvision.models.resnet

title.zh: Dice、IoU、HD95 医学图像分割评价指标详解：公式、代码与解读误区
title.en: Dice, IoU and HD95: Medical Segmentation Metrics Explained with Formulas and Code

description.zh: Dice、IoU、精确率、召回率与 HD95 分别衡量什么，如何用 Python 计算，以及体素间距、空预测、2D 与 3D 平均这些最容易出错的细节。
description.en: What Dice, IoU, precision, recall and HD95 each measure, how to compute them in Python, and the details that go wrong: voxel spacing, empty predictions, 2D vs 3D averaging.

text.zh: 阅读约 7 分钟 读论文时，分割结果几乎都是用 Dice 和 HD95 汇报。两个数字看起来简单，但”怎么算”里藏着很多细节，不同实现可能差好几个点。这篇笔记把常用指标的含义、公式和最容易出错的地方整理在一起。 先分清两类指标 重叠类回答”区域对了多少”，但对边界的细小偏差不敏感。 距离类回答”边界偏了多远”，但容易被孤立的错误点影响。 只报一类会漏掉信息，所以论文通常两类都给。 重叠类指标 以混淆矩阵的 TP（预测与真实都是前景）、FP（误报）、FN（漏报）表示： $$\text{Dice} = \frac{2\ \text{TP}}{2\ \text{TP} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}} \qquad \text{IoU} = \frac{\text{TP}}{\text{TP} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}}$$ $$\text{Precision} = \frac{\text{TP}}{\text{TP} + \text{FP}} \qquad \text{Recall} = \frac{\text{TP}}{\text{TP} + \text{FN}}$$ 精确率回答“预测为前景的里，有多少是对的”，召回率回答“真实前景里，有多少被找到了”。 几个关系值得记住： Dice 与 IoU 是单调关系：$\text{Dice} = \dfrac{2\ \text{IoU}}{1 + \text{IoU}}$。所以 Dice 为 0.9 对应 IoU 约 0.82，同一个模型的排序在两者之间不会反转。 Dice 实际上是 Precision 和 Recall 的调和平均（即 F1）。 用于对比模型时，Precision 和 Recall 能告诉你模型是偏保守还是偏激进：Precision 低说明误报多，Recall 低说明漏掉了目标。 距离类指标：HD95 Hausdorff 距离（HD）取预测边界与真实边界之间所有点距离的最大值。一个孤立的错误点就能让它变得很大，所以实践中更常用 HD95：取第 95 百分位，忽略最差的 5%。 HD95 的单位是体素或毫米，越小越好。要用毫米报告，必须传入体素间距；尤其在层间距明显大于层内分辨率的各向异性数据上，忽略 spacing 会让不同方向的距离失去统一的物理意义。相关背景可以参见 MACM 的动机。 Python 计算 六个最容易出错的细节 2D 切片平均 vs 3D 体积：对每张切片算 Dice 再平均，和对整个体积算一次 Dice，结果可能差很多，因为含很少目标的切片会被同等对待。要说明采用哪种。 空预测或空标注：Dice 在两者都为空时是 0/0；HD95 在任一为空时未定义。要明确用 NaN、跳过，还是赋默认值，并在论文里写明。 体素间距：HD95 必须乘上真实间距，否则数值的单位不统一。 预处理不一致：评估时必须把预测重采样回原始空间，在原始分辨率上算指标，而不是在裁剪、缩放后的图上算。 多类别：逐类报告，不要把背景算进平均（原因与 Dice Loss 里的情况 相同）。 只报告平均值：分割表现常常有几个失败病例拖累。至少同时给出标准差、中位数或箱线图，对比两个模型时用配对检验（如 Wilcoxon 符号秩检验）。 怎样选择报告哪些指标 场景 推荐 通用分割对比 Dice + HD95 关心误报和漏报的平衡 再加 Precision 和 Recall 小目标（病灶） Dice 会很不稳定，补充 HD95 和逐病例结果 临床勾画、放疗计划 补充距离类指标，直接表达边界偏差的毫米数 指标和训练目标不必一致，但要知道它们的盲区：Dice Loss 优化重叠，不直接约束边界；改进特征融合（例如 AFFM 抑制背景噪声）可能改善 HD95，但仍需用实验单独验证。 小结 Dice 和 IoU 回答”重合了多少”，HD95 回答”边界偏了多远”。 同一个模型，换一种平均方式或忽略体素间距，数字就会变。 对比论文数字之前，先确认它们的口径一致。 相关阅读：U-Net 结构详解，医学影像深度学习模型全景。
text.en: 7 min read Segmentation papers almost always report Dice and HD95. The two numbers look simple, but how they are computed hides many details, and different implementations can differ by several points. These notes collect what the common metrics mean, their formulas, and where people trip. Two families of metrics Overlap answers “how much of the region is right” but barely notices small boundary errors. Distance answers “how far off is the boundary” but is easily swayed by isolated bad points. Reporting only one family loses information, so papers usually give both. Overlap metrics Using TP (foreground in both), FP (false alarm) and FN (miss): $$\text{Dice} = \frac{2\ \text{TP}}{2\ \text{TP} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}} \qquad \text{IoU} = \frac{\text{TP}}{\text{TP} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}}$$ $$\text{Precision} = \frac{\text{TP}}{\text{TP} + \text{FP}} \qquad \text{Recall} = \frac{\text{TP}}{\text{TP} + \text{FN}}$$ Precision asks how much of what you predicted is right; recall asks how much of the true foreground you found. Worth remembering: Dice and IoU are monotonically related: $\text{Dice} = \dfrac{2\ \text{IoU}}{1 + \text{IoU}}$. A Dice of 0.9 is an IoU of about 0.82, and model rankings do not flip between them. Dice is the harmonic mean of precision and recall (that is, F1). Precision and recall show whether a model is conservative or aggressive: low precision means many false alarms, low recall means missed targets. Distance metric: HD95 The Hausdorff distance (HD) is the maximum distance between predicted and true boundary points. One isolated bad point can make it huge, so HD95 — the 95th percentile, ignoring the worst 5% — is more common. HD95 is in voxels or millimetres, and lower is better. To report millimetres you must pass the voxel spacing; on anisotropic data (such as prostate MR with 3 mm slices and 0.5 mm in-plane, the motivation for MACM) numbers without spacing have no physical meaning. Python Six details that go wrong 2D slice average vs 3D volume — averaging per-slice Dice and computing one Dice on the volume can differ a lot, since slices with little target count equally. State which one you use. Empty prediction or mask — Dice is 0/0 when both are empty; HD95 is undefined when either is. Decide between NaN, skipping, or a default, and say so. Voxel spacing — HD95 must use the real spacing, or units are inconsistent. Inconsistent preprocessing — resample predictions back to the original space and compute metrics at original resolution, not on cropped or rescaled images. Multi-class — report per class, and keep background out of the average (the same reason as in Dice Loss). Mean only — a few failed cases often drag the result. Give the standard deviation, median or a box plot, and compare two models with a paired test such as Wilcoxon signed-rank. Which metrics to report Setting Recommended General model comparison Dice + HD95 Balance of false alarms and misses Add precision and recall Small targets (lesions) Dice is unstable; add HD95 and per-case results Clinical contouring, radiotherapy planning Distance metrics are closer to what matters; a few mm of boundary error counts more than overlap Metrics need not match the training objective, but know their blind spots: Dice Loss optimises overlap and does not constrain the boundary directly, which is why improvements such as AFFM suppressing background noise often show up in HD95. Summary Dice and IoU say how much overlaps; HD95 says how far the boundary is off. For the same model, a different averaging scheme or ignoring spacing changes the number. Before comparing with a paper’s numbers, confirm the conventions match. Related: U-Net explained, Deep learning models for medical imaging.

title.zh: Dice Loss 公式、代码与常见错误：医学图像分割损失函数详解
title.en: Dice Loss: Formula, Code and Common Mistakes in Medical Image Segmentation

description.zh: Dice Loss 的公式推导、PyTorch 实现，以及 5 个最常见的错误：先阈值再求损失、batch 级与样本级混用、空标注除零、多分类含背景。
description.en: The Dice Loss formula, a PyTorch implementation, and five common mistakes: thresholding before the loss, batch-level vs sample-level, empty masks, and counting background.

text.zh: 阅读约 7 分钟 前列腺、肿瘤、病灶在整张图里往往只占很小一部分。这时如果只看像素准确率，把所有像素都预测成背景也可能得到很高的分数，但分割结果毫无用处。Dice Loss 直接优化前景重叠，适合这种类别极度不平衡的场景；V-Net 原论文也正是为此引入了基于 Dice 系数的训练目标。 从 Dice 系数到 Dice Loss 设 P 是预测区域，G 是真实标注区域： $$\text{Dice} = \frac{2\ |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|} = \frac{2\ \text{TP}}{2\ \text{TP} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}}$$ 取值 0 到 1，完全重合为 1，完全不相交为 0。它只关心前景，所以不会被海量背景像素稀释。 训练时需要可导，所以把硬标签的预测换成概率图，即 soft Dice： $$\hat D = \frac{2 \sum_i p_i g_i + \varepsilon}{\sum_i p_i + \sum_i g_i + \varepsilon} \qquad \mathcal{L} = 1 - \hat D$$ 其中 p 是网络输出的概率，g 是 0/1 的真实标签，smooth 是一个小常数。 PyTorch 实现 二分类，样本级 Dice： 多分类： 五个常见错误 1. 先阈值再求损失 阈值操作几乎处处梯度为零，网络无法通过它正常反向传播。训练时必须用连续概率；阈值化只用于评估。 2. 忘记 Sigmoid 或 Softmax 直接把 logits 放进公式，数值可以是负数或很大，Dice 的取值范围就失效了。如果使用的是已经内置激活的损失库，要确认网络最后一层有没有重复激活。 3. 批级与样本级混用 样本级：每个病例算一个 Dice 再平均，每个病例权重相同，大病灶和小病灶一视同仁。 批级：把整个 batch 拼起来算一次，大病灶主导结果，小病灶容易被忽略。 两种都合理，但要明确选择，并且验证指标的口径要和训练一致。 4. 空标注导致除零或梯度异常 很多切片或病例本身没有前景。分母为 0 时会得到 NaN；加了 smooth 后，如果预测也为空，Dice 等于 1，如果预测非空则接近 0，梯度会出现剧烈变化。 处理办法：保留 smooth，或者只在含前景的样本上计算 Dice，同时配合其他损失。 5. 多分类时把背景算进去 背景像素数量巨大，它的 Dice 几乎总是接近 1，会把平均值抬高，掩盖前景类别的真实表现。多分类时通常排除背景，或者对各类别分别记录。 它的局限，以及常见的搭配 梯度不稳定：目标很小时，分母很小，梯度会很大，训练曲线抖动。 只衡量重叠：对边界形状不敏感，需要 HD95 等指标 补充。 不直接优化概率校准：Dice Loss 的目标是提高区域重叠，不能仅凭它的输出值判断置信度是否可靠。 实践中常用 Dice + 交叉熵 的组合：交叉熵提供稳定的逐像素梯度，Dice 负责缓解类别不平衡。更准确地说，nnU-Net v2 的默认普通类别任务使用等权 Dice + 交叉熵；如果采用区域标签训练，则使用 Dice + BCE。 小结 问题 选择 前景占比极小 Dice Loss 或 Dice + 交叉熵 训练不稳定 加大 smooth，或加入交叉熵 有大量空标注 保留 smooth，统计时单独处理空样本 多分类 排除背景，逐类记录 Dice 更多关于网络结构的内容，可以继续阅读 U-Net 结构详解；如果想看这些损失函数最终怎样被用于论文里的实验，参考 MM-UNet 整体架构。 资料来源：V-Net 原论文（提出基于 Dice 的训练目标） · nnU-Net v2 默认损失实现
text.en: 7 min read A prostate, a tumour or a lesion often covers only a small part of the image — the foreground can be under 5% of the pixels. With plain per-pixel cross-entropy, a network that predicts everything as background already scores over 95% accuracy while producing a useless mask. Dice Loss is built for this extreme class imbalance, and it was popularised for 3D medical segmentation by V-Net. From the Dice coefficient to Dice Loss Let P be the predicted region and G the ground truth: $$\text{Dice} = \frac{2\ |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|} = \frac{2\ \text{TP}}{2\ \text{TP} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}}$$ It runs from 0 to 1 — 1 for a perfect match, 0 for no overlap — and it ignores the huge background, so background cannot dilute it. For training it must be differentiable, so hard predictions become probabilities: soft Dice. $$\hat D = \frac{2 \sum_i p_i g_i + \varepsilon}{\sum_i p_i + \sum_i g_i + \varepsilon} \qquad \mathcal{L} = 1 - \hat D$$ p is the network’s probability, g the 0/1 ground truth, smooth a small constant. PyTorch implementation Binary, per-sample Dice: Multi-class: Five common mistakes 1. Thresholding before the loss The gradient of a threshold is zero, so nothing is learned. Train on probabilities; threshold only for evaluation. 2. Forgetting sigmoid or softmax Feeding raw logits into the formula gives negative or huge values and the Dice range stops holding. If you use a library loss with a built-in activation, check the last layer does not apply it twice. 3. Mixing batch-level and sample-level Sample-level: one Dice per case, then average — every case counts equally, big lesion or small. Batch-level: pool the whole batch and compute once — large lesions dominate and small ones are neglected. Both are reasonable, but choose deliberately, and keep the validation metric consistent with training. 4. Empty masks Many slices or cases have no foreground. A zero denominator gives NaN; with smooth, an empty prediction scores 1 while a non-empty one scores near 0, so the gradient swings sharply. Keep smooth, or compute Dice only on samples that have foreground and add another loss. 5. Counting background in multi-class Background has a huge pixel count and its Dice is almost always near 1, lifting the average and hiding how the foreground classes really do. Exclude it, or log each class separately. Limits, and common pairings Unstable gradients — with a tiny target the denominator is small and gradients get large, so the loss curve jitters. Overlap only — it is insensitive to boundary shape; add HD95 and similar metrics. Poor calibration — Dice Loss pushes outputs to 0 or 1, so the probabilities are no longer trustworthy. In practice Dice + cross-entropy is common: cross-entropy supplies stable per-pixel gradients and Dice counters the imbalance. nnU-Net uses this combination by default. Summary Situation Choice Tiny foreground Dice Loss or Dice + cross-entropy Unstable training Larger smooth, or add cross-entropy Many empty masks Keep smooth; report empty cases separately Multi-class Exclude background, log Dice per class For the network side, continue with U-Net explained; for a full model that uses these ideas, see the MM-UNet overview. Source: V-Net: Fully Convolutional Neural Networks for Volumetric Medical Image Segmentation

title.zh: U-Net 结构详解：编码器、跳跃连接与解码器如何做医学图像分割
title.en: U-Net Explained: Encoder, Skip Connections and Decoder for Medical Image Segmentation

description.zh: U-Net 为什么是医学图像分割的起点：编码器压缩语义、解码器恢复分辨率，跳跃连接把边界细节送回来，以及 3D U-Net 与 nnU-Net 的演化。
description.en: Why U-Net is where medical segmentation starts: the encoder compresses meaning, the decoder restores resolution, skip connections bring boundary detail back — plus 3D U-Net and nnU-Net.

text.zh: 阅读约 7 分钟 做医学图像分割，几乎绕不开 U-Net。它用对称的编码器—解码器和跳跃连接，把全局语义与像素级定位结合起来，后来成为医学图像分割最具代表性的基础架构之一。MM-UNet 以及许多 CNN、Transformer 分割模型，都沿用了或改造了这种 U 形思路。 它要解决什么问题 分割要求为每个像素输出类别，需要同时满足两件互相冲突的事： 知道这是什么：需要深层的、感受野很大的抽象语义特征。 知道边界在哪：需要浅层的、分辨率很高的细节特征。 分类网络一路下采样，丢掉了位置细节；只用高分辨率特征，又看不到整体。U-Net 的答案是：先压缩拿语义，再放大恢复分辨率，并且把压缩之前的细节通过”捷径”直接送回来。 整体结构 紫色路径压缩空间并提取语义，绿色路径恢复分辨率；金色连线把同尺度的边界细节直接送入解码器。 三个部分 编码器（收缩路径） 每一级由两个 3x3 卷积加 ReLU 组成，随后用 2x2 最大池化把空间尺寸减半，同时把通道数翻倍。原论文图 1 明确给出了 64、128、256、512、1024 五级通道数，也就是连续下采样 4 次。 随着分辨率下降，每个位置的感受野越来越大，表达的信息也从边缘、纹理逐渐变成器官和区域。 解码器（扩张路径） 每一级先用上采样（原论文是 2x2 转置卷积）把分辨率翻倍、通道数减半，再和编码器同尺度特征拼接，最后经过两个 3x3 卷积。 跳跃连接 这是 U-Net 最关键的设计。编码器第 k 级的输出，不仅送给下一级继续压缩，也直接送到解码器同尺度的位置，沿通道维度拼接： $$\text{decoder input} = \mathrm{concat}\bigl( \mathrm{upsample}(F_{\text{deep}}),\ E_k \bigr)$$ 上采样得到的特征语义强但边界模糊，编码器特征边界精细但语义弱，拼接之后，后面的卷积就能同时参考两者。 为什么小数据集也能训练 原论文的电子显微镜实验只有 30 张完整标注的训练图像。它主要依靠两点提高数据利用率： 强数据增强：尤其是弹性形变，模拟组织的自然变形，让网络从很少的图像里学到更多变化。 密集的像素级监督：每张标注图像都提供整幅分割图上的监督信号；这些像素并非彼此独立，但信息密度仍高于只给一个图像级标签。 跳跃连接的局限，以及后续改进 跳跃连接也有代价：编码器的浅层特征里混有大量背景噪声，直接拼接会把噪声一起送进解码器。 后续工作大多围绕这里展开： 改进方向 代表思路 对应内容 筛选跳跃特征 先用通道注意力给低层特征打权重再融合 MM-UNet 的 AFFM，原理同 SENet 更密集的连接 让特征在多级之间复用 DenseNet 的拼接思想 更强的全局建模 在瓶颈处加入 Transformer 或 Mamba MM-UNet 的 GCM 适配 3D 数据 3D 卷积，或各向异性卷积 MACM 从 2D 到 3D，再到 nnU-Net 3D U-Net：把 2D 卷积和池化换成 3D 版本，直接处理 CT、MRI 体数据。代价是显存和参数量上升很快，可以对照 参数量 与 GFLOPs 估算。 nnU-Net：它的主要贡献不是新模块，而是一套能根据数据集自动确定预处理、网络深度、patch 大小和训练策略的流程。在很多医学分割基准上，一个调得好的 U-Net 仍是很强的基线。 实现时容易出错的地方 拼接前尺寸不一致：卷积不加 padding 时，编码器特征比解码器大，需要裁剪；现代实现通常用 same padding 避免这件事。 通道数写错：拼接后通道数是两者之和，下一个卷积的输入通道要相应修改。 归一化选择不合适：原论文没有 BatchNorm；现代实现常加入 BatchNorm 或 InstanceNorm，小 batch 的 3D 任务通常更适合考虑 InstanceNorm。 损失函数选择：前景占比很小时，单独的交叉熵容易被背景主导，通常配合 Dice Loss。 只看 Dice 就下结论：边界质量需要用 HD95 等指标 补充。 U-Net 的价值在于一种思路：先压缩得到理解，再把压缩前的细节带回来。后来大多数分割网络，都是在回答”带回来的细节该怎么挑”。 资料来源：U-Net 原论文（含图 1 的通道数与结构） · 3D U-Net 原论文 · nnU-Net 论文 · nnU-Net 官方实现
text.en: 7 min read Almost every medical segmentation paper starts from U-Net. It was not the first fully convolutional segmentation network, but it made pixel-accurate boundaries from a small dataset an ordinary thing. MM-UNet and most Transformer-based segmenters are this U-shaped skeleton with one part replaced or strengthened. The problem it solves Segmentation labels every pixel, and that needs two things that pull against each other: Knowing what it is — deep features with a large receptive field. Knowing where the boundary is — shallow, high-resolution features. A classifier keeps downsampling and loses position. High-resolution features alone cannot see the whole object. U-Net’s answer: compress to gain meaning, expand to restore resolution, and send the pre-compression detail back through shortcuts. Overall structure The lavender path compresses space and learns semantics; the sage path restores resolution, while gold links return same-scale boundary detail to the decoder. The three parts Encoder (contracting path) Each level has two 3x3 convolutions with ReLU, then 2x2 max pooling halves the spatial size while the channel count doubles. In the original paper channels grow from 64 to 1024 over four downsamplings. As resolution drops, each position sees more of the image, and what it represents shifts from edges and texture to organs and regions. Decoder (expanding path) Each level upsamples (a 2x2 transposed convolution in the paper) to double the resolution and halve the channels, concatenates the encoder features of the same scale, and applies two 3x3 convolutions. Skip connections This is the key design. The output of encoder level k goes both to the next level and directly to the decoder at the same scale, joined along the channel axis: $$\text{decoder input} = \mathrm{concat}\bigl( \mathrm{upsample}(F_{\text{deep}}),\ E_k \bigr)$$ Upsampled features are semantically strong but blurry at the edges; encoder features have sharp edges but little semantics. After concatenation the following convolutions can use both. Why it trains on tiny datasets The original paper had only a few dozen annotated images. It leaned on two things: Heavy augmentation, especially elastic deformation, which mimics natural tissue deformation and squeezes more variety out of few images. Every pixel is a training sample, so supervision per image is far denser than for image-level classification. Limits of skip connections, and what followed Shallow encoder features carry a lot of background noise, and concatenating them passes that noise on to the decoder. Most later work targets exactly this: Direction Idea See Filter the skip features Weight low-level features with channel attention before fusing AFFM in MM-UNet, same principle as SENet Denser connections Reuse features across many levels the concatenation idea in DenseNet Stronger global modelling Put a Transformer or Mamba at the bottleneck GCM in MM-UNet Fit 3D data 3D convolutions or anisotropic ones MACM From 2D to 3D, and nnU-Net 3D U-Net swaps 2D convolutions and pooling for 3D ones and works directly on CT and MRI volumes. Memory and parameters grow fast; compare parameter count and GFLOPs to estimate the cost. nnU-Net‘s main contribution is not a new block but a pipeline that configures preprocessing, depth, patch size and training from the dataset itself. On many medical benchmarks a well-tuned U-Net is still a very strong baseline. Where implementations go wrong Mismatched sizes before concatenation — without padding the encoder map is larger than the decoder’s and must be cropped; modern code uses same-padding to avoid this. Wrong channel counts — after concatenation the channels are the sum of both inputs, so the next convolution’s input must change. Forgetting normalisation — the paper had no BatchNorm; practical implementations add BatchNorm or, for small-batch 3D work, InstanceNorm. Choice of loss — with a small foreground, plain cross-entropy is dominated by background; it is usually paired with Dice Loss. Judging by Dice alone — boundary quality needs metrics such as HD95. U-Net’s value is an idea: compress to understand, then bring back the detail you compressed away. Most later segmentation networks are answers to “which detail should come back?” Source: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation

title.zh: GFLOPs 怎么计算？卷积层 FLOPs 公式及其与参数量的区别
title.en: How to Calculate GFLOPs: Convolution FLOPs Formula vs. Parameter Count

description.zh: GFLOPs 到底在数什么：卷积层浮点运算量的推导，以及它和参数量为什么不是一回事。
description.en: Where the number comes from, and why it is not the same thing as parameter count.

text.zh: 阅读约 3 分钟 核心定义 FLOPs：浮点运算次数。指模型进行一次前向推理（即处理一张输入图片）所需完成的浮点数加法和乘法运算的总次数。 GFLOPs：十亿次浮点运算。$1\ \text{GFLOPs} = 10^9\ \text{FLOPs}$。为了方便表示，我们通常用 GFLOPs 来描述模型的运算量级。 简单类比： 参数量：像是一本字典的页数（静态的、存储占用的大小）。 GFLOPs：像是查完这本字典所有单词所需翻阅的总次数（动态的、完成一次任务所需的工作量）。 为什么它重要？ 在轻量化模型中，低GFLOPs意味着： 推理速度更快：完成一次预测所需时间更短。 功耗更低：对电池供电的设备（如手机）至关重要。 发热更少：有利于设备长期稳定运行。 更适合实时应用：如内镜下的实时病灶分割。 在您论文的图1中，颜色深度代表GFLOPs，就是为了直观展示：即使两个模型参数量相近，它们的计算开销也可能天差地别。 GFLOPs是如何计算出来的？ 计算基础是 “乘-加”运算。在硬件中，一次 $y = wx + b$ 这样的操作通常被计为 1次浮点运算（尽管它包含一次乘法和一次加法）。 我们以最耗计算资源的卷积层为例，讲解其FLOPs的计算公式： 对于一个卷积层，假设： 输入特征图尺寸：$H_{\text{in}} \times W_{\text{in}} \times C_{\text{in}}$ 输出特征图尺寸：$H_{\text{out}} \times W_{\text{out}} \times C_{\text{out}}$ 卷积核尺寸：$K \times K$ 偏置：有（通常为 True） 计算过程分为两步： 计算单个输出像素点的FLOPs： 为了得到一个输出像素，需要将 $K \times K \times C_{\text{in}}$ 个权重与对应的输入窗口进行逐元素相乘并累加。 这相当于 $K \times K \times C_{\text{in}}$ 次乘法和 $K \times K \times C_{\text{in}} - 1$ 次加法。 如果考虑偏置，还需要再加1次加法。 通常，我们将一次“乘加”计为 1次FLOP。因此，得到一个输出像素的FLOPs约为：$$F_{\text{pixel}} \approx 2 \times K \times K \times C_{\text{in}}$$ 计算该卷积层的总FLOPs： 将单个像素的运算量乘以输出特征图的总像素数。 同时，每个输出通道都有一个独立的卷积核（滤波器）。 因此，单层卷积的总FLOPs公式为：$$F_{\text{conv}} = 2 \times C_{\text{out}} \times H_{\text{out}} \times W_{\text{out}} \times \bigl( C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K \bigr)$$ 公式解读： $C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K$：处理一个输入通道的一个输出像素所需的计算量。 $H_{\text{out}} \times W_{\text{out}}$：输出特征图的空间尺寸（像素总数）。 $C_{\text{out}}$：输出通道数（滤波器数量）。 前面的 $\times 2$：对应每次乘加运算（1 次乘加 1 次加）。 注意：有时在论文中，为了简化，会将乘加直接计为1次操作，此时公式中的 $\times 2$ 会消失。关键在于对比时需统一标准。您论文中的GFLOPs颜色条，只要所有模型采用同一标准计算，其相对比较就是有意义的。
text.en: 5 min read Definitions FLOPs — floating point operations. The total number of floating-point multiplications and additions needed for one forward pass, that is, to process one input. GFLOPs — one billion FLOPs. $1\ \text{GFLOPs} = 10^9\ \text{FLOPs}$. The analogy I use: Parameter count is the number of pages in a dictionary — static, and it tells you how much storage it occupies. GFLOPs is how many page-turns it takes to look up every word — dynamic, and it tells you how much work one task costs. Why it matters For a lightweight model, low GFLOPs means: Faster inference — less time per prediction. Lower power — critical on battery-powered devices. Less heat — better for sustained operation. Real-time feasibility — for example, live lesion segmentation during endoscopy. When a paper’s figure uses colour depth to encode GFLOPs, the point is usually this: two models with similar parameter counts can still have wildly different compute costs. How it is calculated The basic unit is the multiply-accumulate. In hardware, $y = wx + b$ is usually counted as one floating-point operation, even though it contains both a multiply and an add. Take a convolutional layer — normally the most expensive part: Input feature map: $H_{\text{in}} \times W_{\text{in}} \times C_{\text{in}}$ Output feature map: $H_{\text{out}} \times W_{\text{out}} \times C_{\text{out}}$ Kernel: K × K Bias: present Step one — one output pixel. Producing a single output value means multiplying K × K × C_in weights with the matching input window and summing them. That is K × K × C_in multiplications and (K × K × C_in − 1) additions, plus one more for the bias. Counting a multiply-accumulate as one FLOP: $$F_{\text{pixel}} \approx 2 \times K \times K \times C_{\text{in}}$$ Step two — the whole layer. Multiply by the number of output pixels, and by the number of filters: $$F_{\text{conv}} = 2 \times C_{\text{out}} \times H_{\text{out}} \times W_{\text{out}} \times \bigl( C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K \bigr)$$ Reading the formula: Term What it counts $C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K$ Work for one output pixel in one channel $H_{\text{out}} \times W_{\text{out}}$ Number of output positions C_out Number of filters × 2 The multiply and the add The caveat Some papers count a multiply-accumulate as one operation rather than two, which drops the factor of 2 and halves every number. Neither convention is wrong — but a comparison is only meaningful if every model in it was measured the same way. When reading a figure, the relative ordering is trustworthy; the absolute values are only as trustworthy as the stated convention.

title.zh: 深度学习模型参数量怎么计算？卷积层与全连接层公式详解
title.en: How to Calculate Deep Learning Model Parameters: Convolutional and Fully Connected Layer Formulas

description.zh: 逐层拆解参数量的计算方式，并解释卷积的参数共享为什么让它比全连接层轻得多。
description.en: Counting weights per layer, and why convolution's weight sharing keeps it so much lighter than a dense layer.

text.zh: 阅读约 3 分钟 在深度学习和模型轻量化领域，“参数个数”是一个衡量模型大小、复杂度和内存占用的关键指标。 简单来说，参数个数就是模型中所有需要通过学习（训练）来确定的数值的总数。这些数值决定了模型如何对输入数据进行转换和预测。 下面从几个层面详细解释： 一、参数是什么？ 模型参数主要包括： 权重：连接神经元之间的强度值。 偏置：为神经元提供基础的激活阈值。 训练过程就是通过大量数据，不断调整这些权重和偏置，使得模型的输出尽可能接近正确答案。 二、参数是如何计算出来的？（按层解析） 参数的数量不涉及输入数据，只由**模型自身的结构（架构）**决定。我们通过计算每一层的参数，然后求和得到总量。 1. 全连接层 这是最直观的。如果一层有 $m$ 个输入神经元和 $n$ 个输出神经元，那么： 权重数 $= m n$（每个输入和每个输出之间都有一个连接权重） 偏置数 $= n$（每个输出神经元有一个偏置） $$P_{\text{fc}} = m n + n$$ 举例：一个输入为1000维，输出为500维的全连接层，其参数为 $1000 \times 500 + 500 = 500{,}500$。可以看到，全连接层的参数增长非常快，是导致模型臃肿的主因之一。 2. 卷积层 卷积层的参数与输入图像大小无关，只与卷积核的大小、数量和深度有关。对于一个卷积层，假设： 输入通道数为 $C_{\text{in}}$ 输出通道数（即卷积核数量）为 $C_{\text{out}}$ 卷积核尺寸为 $K \times K$（例如 $3 \times 3$） 那么： 每个卷积核的参数：一个卷积核要处理输入的所有通道，所以单个卷积核的权重数为 $C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K$，加上 1 个偏置。 该层总参数：因为有 $C_{\text{out}}$ 个卷积核，所以： $$P_{\text{conv}} = C_{\text{out}} \times \bigl( C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K + 1 \bigr)$$ 举例：一个卷积层，输入通道为3（RGB图像），输出通道为64，使用3x3卷积核。参数为 $64 \times (3 \times 3 \times 3 + 1) = 64 \times 28 = 1{,}792$。 这正是卷积神经网络相对轻量的原因：参数共享。一个3x3的卷积核可以滑动检测整张图片的特征，而不需要像全连接层那样为每个像素位置都设置独立的权重。 3. 归一化层、池化层 批量归一化层：有可学习的缩放参数 $\gamma$ 和偏移参数 $\beta$，每个通道一对。如果通道数为 $C$，则参数为 $2C$。这个数量通常很少。 池化层：没有可学习的参数。它只是执行一个固定的计算规则（如取最大值、求平均值）。 三、如何与您提供的文本和图1联系起来？ 在您提到的轻量级皮肤病变分割的上下文中： UNeXt 为何能“减少参数”？ 传统的U-Net使用大量卷积层。UNeXt用 “tokenized MLP块” 替代了部分卷积操作。 MLP（多层感知机）本质上是全连接层，但UNeXt的关键在于“tokenization”和局部MLP。它将特征图分割成局部小块（token），在每个小块内部或小块之间进行轻量级的MLP计算。 这样做避免了传统卷积堆叠带来的通道数爆炸性增长，也避免了全局全连接层的巨大参数量，从而在整体上实现了参数量的显著降低。 为什么图1用“参数个数”作为X轴？ 参数量直接决定模型大小：参数量越少，模型文件越小（例如从几百MB降到几MB），越容易部署到手机、边缘设备。 间接影响速度和能耗：参数少的模型，推理时需要移动的内存数据也少，通常计算量（GFLOPs）也更低，因此更快、更省电。 展示“权衡”关系：图1的目的就是展示，在追求轻量化（X轴向左）的同时，如何尽可能保持高精度（Y轴向上）。这是一个核心的工程与科研权衡。 四、在实际中如何获知参数量？ 研究人员和工程师不需要手动计算每一层。常用的深度学习框架都提供了简单的函数来统计总参数量： PyTorch: sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) TensorFlow/Keras: model.count_params()
text.en: 6 min read In deep learning and model compression, parameter count is the standard measure of a model’s size, complexity and memory footprint. Put simply: it is the total number of values the model has to learn. Those values determine how the model transforms its input into a prediction. What counts as a parameter Weights — the connection strengths between units. Biases — the baseline activation offset for each unit. Training is the process of adjusting those two things, over many examples, until the output is close enough to the right answer. Counting them, layer by layer Parameter count does not depend on the input data at all. It is determined entirely by the model’s own architecture. Fully connected layer With m input units and n output units: Weights = $m \times n$ — every input connects to every output. Biases = n — one per output unit. Total = $m n + n$ For a layer from 1000 dimensions to 500: $$1000 \times 500 + 500 = 500{,}500$$ Dense layers grow fast. They are one of the main reasons models become bloated. Convolutional layer Crucially, this does not depend on the input image size — only on the kernel. Input channels: C_in Output channels (number of filters): C_out Kernel: K × K Each filter must span all input channels, so one filter holds $C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K$ weights plus one bias: $$P_{\text{conv}} = C_{\text{out}} \times \bigl( C_{\text{in}} \times K \times K + 1 \bigr)$$ For 3 input channels (RGB), 64 output channels, 3×3 kernel: $$64 \times (3 \times 3 \times 3 + 1) = 64 \times 28 = 1{,}792$$ This is exactly why convolutional networks are comparatively light: weight sharing. One 3×3 kernel slides across the whole image to detect a feature, instead of a dense layer needing separate weights for every pixel position. Normalisation and pooling Layer Parameters Batch normalisation $2C$ — a scale γ and a shift β per channel Pooling None — it applies a fixed rule such as max or average Batch norm’s contribution is real but usually small. Why papers plot parameters on the x-axis In the lightweight segmentation literature — UNeXt and similar — figures typically put parameter count on the x-axis and accuracy on the y-axis. Two reasons: Parameters determine model size directly. Fewer parameters means a smaller file, which is what makes deployment to a phone or an edge device possible at all — the difference between hundreds of megabytes and a few. They correlate with speed and energy. Fewer parameters usually means less data movement during inference, which usually means lower GFLOPs, faster execution and less power. The figure exists to show the trade-off: how far left can you move without falling down the y-axis. How UNeXt reduces parameters It replaces some convolutional stages with tokenised MLP blocks. The key is the tokenisation plus locality: the feature map is split into local patches, and lightweight MLP computation happens within or between those patches. That avoids both the channel explosion of stacked convolutions and the enormous cost of a global dense layer. Just measure it Nobody counts by hand: The part worth internalising Parameter count and GFLOPs answer different questions. Parameters tell you how big the model is; GFLOPs tell you how much work one prediction costs. A model can be small and slow, or large and fast. Reporting only one of them hides half the picture.

title.zh: SENet 通道注意力详解：Squeeze-and-Excitation 原理与计算过程
title.en: SENet Channel Attention Explained: Squeeze-and-Excitation Principles and Computation

description.zh: Squeeze-and-Excitation：用全局平均池化加两层全连接，为每个通道学出一个重要性权重。
description.en: Squeeze to a vector, excite through two dense layers, then rescale every channel. A small block that keeps showing up everywhere.

text.zh: 阅读约 3 分钟 论文信息 论文标题: Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks 论文链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01507 官方代码: GitHub - hujie-frank/SENet PyTorch实现: GitHub - miraclewkf/SENet-PyTorch 一、SENet概述 竞赛成绩 SENet在ImageNet 2017竞赛图像分类任务中夺冠，取得突破性成果： 原最佳成绩: 2.991% (top-5 error) SENet成绩: 2.251% (top-5 error) 提升幅度: 0.74% 绝对提升 核心思想 研究动机: 显式建模特征通道间的相互依赖关系 技术策略: 采用”特征重标定”策略，避免引入新的空间维度 工作机制: 通过网络学习自动获取每个特征通道的重要程度 实现方式: 提升有用特征通道权重，抑制次要特征通道权重 架构特点 模块化设计: SE block作为子结构，可嵌入现有网络 端到端训练: 完全可微分，支持端到端优化 即插即用: 灵活集成到各种分类和检测网络 二、SENet结构组成详解 SE模块完整流程 输入特征 → 常规卷积变换 → Squeeze操作 → Excitation操作 → Reweight操作 → 输出特征↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ H×W×C₁ H×W×C₂ 1×1×C₂ 1×1×C₂ H×W×C₂ 1. 常规变换 (Ftr) $$u_c = v_c * X = \sum_{s=1}^{C_1} v_c^s * x^s$$ 操作类型: 标准卷积变换 输入维度: $H \times W \times C_1$ 输出维度: $H \times W \times C_2$ 功能说明: 基础特征提取，不属于SE核心创新 2. Squeeze操作 (特征压缩) $$z_c = F_{\text{sq}}(u_c) = \frac{1}{H \times W} \sum_{i=1}^{H} \sum_{j=1}^{W} u_c(i, j)$$ 操作类型: 全局平均池化(Global Average Pooling) 输入维度: $H \times W \times C_2$ 输出维度: $1 \times 1 \times C_2$ 功能特点: 获取通道级全局感受野 压缩空间维度，保留通道信息 为后续通道权重学习提供全局上下文 3. Excitation操作 (自适应重标定) $$s = F_{\text{ex}}(z, W) = \sigma\bigl( W_2 \ \delta(W_1 z) \bigr)$$ 网络结构: 两全连接层瓶颈结构 参数配置: 缩放比率 $r = 16$ 详细流程: 设计优势: 引入非线性，更好拟合通道相关性 大幅减少参数量和计算量 输出0-1归一化权重 4. Reweight操作 (特征重加权) $$\tilde x_c = F_{\text{scale}}(u_c, s_c) = s_c \cdot u_c$$ 操作类型: 通道级乘法(Channel-wise Multiplication) 实现方式: 每个特征图乘以对应的通道权重 最终效果: 增强重要特征，抑制次要特征 三、SENet在具体网络中应用 Inception网络集成方案 ResNet网络集成方案 网络集成设计原则 网络类型 SE模块位置 设计考虑 Inception系列 模块内部 直接增强特征表达 ResNet系列 残差分支 避免梯度消失问题 其他网络 关键模块后 平衡计算量与性能 支持的SENet变体 SE-BN-Inception SE-ResNet SE-ReNeXt SE-Inception-ResNet-v2 四、SENet计算量分析 参数增加量理论计算 单SE模块参数量 $$P_{\text{single}} = 2 \times \frac{C^2}{r}$$ 整体网络参数量增加 $$\Delta P_{\text{total}} = \frac{2}{r} \sum_{s=1}^{S} N_s \cdot C_s^2$$ 参数说明表 符号 含义 典型值 $C$ 通道数 随网络层变化 $r$ 缩放比率 16 $S$ 网络stage数量 4(ResNet) $N_s$ 第s个stage的block数 随网络深度变化 实际网络参数对比 ResNet-50 vs SE-ResNet-50 指标 ResNet-50 SE-ResNet-50 增长幅度 总参数量 ~25M ~27.5M +10% 计算量 ~4G FLOPs ~4.2G FLOPs +5% 参数优化策略 问题: 最后stage通道数大(2048)，参数增长显著 解决方案: 移除最后stage中部分SE模块 优化效果: 参数量增长从10%降至2%，精度几乎无损
text.en: 7 min read Notes on Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks. Paper: arXiv:1709.01507 Official code: hujie-frank/SENet Why it mattered SENet won the ImageNet 2017 classification task: Top-5 error Previous best 2.991% SENet 2.251% Improvement 0.74 percentage points The idea: model the interdependencies between feature channels explicitly. Rather than adding a new spatial dimension, it recalibrates the channels it already has — the network learns how important each channel is, then amplifies the useful ones and suppresses the rest. It is modular, fully differentiable, and drops into existing architectures without redesign. The four steps 1. Transformation $$u_c = v_c * X = \sum_{s=1}^{C_1} v_c^s * x^s$$ An ordinary convolution from $H \times W \times C_1$ to $H \times W \times C_2$. Not part of the innovation — just the layer SE attaches to. 2. Squeeze $$z_c = F_{\text{sq}}(u_c) = \frac{1}{H \times W} \sum_{i=1}^{H} \sum_{j=1}^{W} u_c(i, j)$$ Global average pooling reduces $H \times W \times C_2$ to $1 \times 1 \times C_2$. Each channel becomes one number summarising its global response. This is what gives a channel-level receptive field over the entire image. 3. Excitation $$s = F_{\text{ex}}(z, W) = \sigma\bigl( W_2 \ \delta(W_1 z) \bigr)$$ A two-layer bottleneck with reduction ratio $r = 16$: The bottleneck adds non-linearity so the model can fit genuine channel correlations, while keeping the parameter cost low. The sigmoid produces weights in 0–1 — importantly not a softmax, because channels are not mutually exclusive. 4. Reweight $$\tilde x_c = F_{\text{scale}}(u_c, s_c) = s_c \cdot u_c$$ Channel-wise multiplication. Important channels are strengthened, minor ones attenuated. Where to place the block Architecture SE position Why Inception family Inside the module Directly strengthens the feature representation ResNet family On the residual branch, before the addition Keeps the identity path clean so gradients still flow Others After a key module Balance cost against benefit Placing SE on the residual branch rather than after the addition is the detail that matters most — putting it after the merge would scale the identity shortcut too, which defeats the point of having one. Known variants: SE-BN-Inception, SE-ResNet, SE-ResNeXt, SE-Inception-ResNet-v2. The cost Parameters added by one SE block: $$P_{\text{single}} = 2 \times \frac{C^2}{r}$$ Over a whole network: $$\Delta P_{\text{total}} = \frac{2}{r} \sum_{s=1}^{S} N_s \cdot C_s^2$$ Symbol Meaning Typical value C Channel count Varies by layer r Reduction ratio 16 S Number of stages 4 in ResNet N_s Blocks in stage s Varies with depth Measured on ResNet-50: Metric ResNet-50 SE-ResNet-50 Increase Parameters ~25M ~27.5M +10% Compute ~4G FLOPs ~4.2G FLOPs +5% Because cost scales with C², the final stage — where C reaches 2048 — dominates. Removing SE from some of those last blocks drops the parameter overhead from 10% to about 2% with almost no accuracy loss. A good reminder that where you place a module matters as much as whether you use it. Why it stayed relevant SE is essentially the simplest possible attention: no spatial dimension, no extra branch topology, two small dense layers. It reappears constantly — including inside USE-Net for prostate segmentation, which is where I first ran into it.

title.zh: DenseNet 网络详解：密集连接、Growth Rate 与参数效率
title.en: DenseNet Explained: Dense Connections, Growth Rate, and Parameter Efficiency

description.zh: 密集连接为什么优于加法融合：拼接保留特征的独立性，Growth Rate 则是可控的复杂度节流阀。
description.en: Addition mixes features irreversibly; concatenation keeps every earlier feature available. That one difference explains most of the architecture.

text.zh: 阅读约 5 分钟 📌 核心思想与设计哲学 1. 三种网络结构对比 2. 信息流本质区别 ResNet（接力赛跑模式）： DenseNet（团队头脑风暴模式）： 🏗️ 架构详解 1. 完整的DenseNet数据流 具体尺寸变化示例： 2. Dense Block内部工作机制 3. 通道增长的具体数学 🔑 关键技术细节 1. Bottleneck Layer的精确作用 位置：在Dense Block内部，每个3x3卷积之前目的：临时压缩通道数，优化计算效率 2. Transition Layer vs Bottleneck 组件 位置 主要作用 是否改变尺寸 是否永久改变通道 Bottleneck Dense Block内部 临时压缩通道，优化3x3卷积计算 ❌ 不变 ❌ 临时压缩 Transition Dense Block之间 永久压缩通道，控制模型增长 ✅ 尺寸减半 ✅ 永久压缩 3. 拼接(concat) vs 加法(add)的本质区别 加法（ResNet）： 拼接（DenseNet）： 🎯 在医学影像中的特殊价值 1. 特征复用优势 多尺度特征同时可用：低级边缘特征 + 中级形状特征 + 高级语义特征 避免信息丢失：原始特征始终可用，不会在深度传递中被”遗忘” 梯度流动优化：浅层直接连接到深层，缓解梯度消失 2. 针对医学图像的特性适配 3. 实际配置建议 ⚡ 训练与优化技巧 1. 内存优化策略 2. 医学数据特殊处理 🔄 与其他模型的对比理解 1. 信息保留能力对比 模型 信息流模式 特征保留 梯度流动 参数效率 传统CNN 替换式 差 容易消失 中等 ResNet 加法融合 中等 较好 较好 DenseNet 拼接累积 优秀 优秀 优秀 2. 在医学影像任务中的选择指南 💡 关键洞察总结 1. 核心创新点 密集连接：不是重复计算，而是智能的特征复用 拼接操作：保持特征独立性，优于加法融合 Growth Rate：人为控制的”节流阀”，精确控制模型复杂度 模块化设计：Bottleneck优化计算，Transition控制增长 2. 在医学影像中的独特价值 特征永不丢失：原始医学特征始终可用，适合细微结构分析 多尺度智能组合：自动综合利用不同抽象层次的特征 高参数效率：在数据有限的医学任务中尤为重要 3. 实用要点 Bottleneck在Block内，Transition在Block间 每个Dense Block独立累积通道数，Transition负责重置 拼接保留所有信息，加法会混合信息 Growth Rate是人为超参数，完全可控设计
text.en: 10 min read Notes on Densely Connected Convolutional Networks, read with medical imaging in mind. Three ways to pass information forward The difference is easiest to hold as two images. ResNet is a relay race. A runs, hands over to B, leaves the track. Only the current runner is present. DenseNet is a standing panel. A contributes, then B joins A, then C joins both. Every earlier expert stays in the room. Architecture A worked example of the sizes: Inside a Dense Block The channel arithmetic is completely predictable: So the channel count grows linearly, not multiplicatively: $$C_l = C_0 + k \cdot l$$ with $C_0$ the initial channels and $k$ the growth rate. Growth rate is a deliberate throttle. Each layer adds only a small, fixed number of new feature maps, so depth does not cause an explosion. Bottleneck and Transition are different things Bottleneck sits inside a Dense Block, before each 3×3 convolution, and compresses channels temporarily. At layer 6, with 224 input channels and a growth rate of 32: Convolutions Multiply-adds Without bottleneck $224 \times 32 \times 3 \times 3$ 64,512 With bottleneck $224 \times 128 \times 1 \times 1$ 28,672 $128 \times 32 \times 3 \times 3$ 36,864 total 65,536 The totals are similar, but the expensive 3×3 operation shrinks considerably and the memory access pattern improves. Component Position Purpose Changes size? Changes channels? Bottleneck Inside a Dense Block Temporarily compress channels for the 3×3 No Temporarily Transition Between Dense Blocks Permanently compress and downsample Yes, halved Yes, permanently Why concatenation beats addition Addition mixes values irreversibly. $$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \cr 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \cr 7 & 8 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 8 \cr 10 & 12 \end{bmatrix}$$ Like mixing paint — the original colours cannot be recovered. Concatenation keeps them side by side. $$A\ (2\ \text{channels}) \ \Vert \ B\ (2\ \text{channels}) \ = \ 4\ \text{channels}$$ Like arranging paints on a palette — each stays independent and usable. Why this matters for medical imaging Medical image property What DenseNet offers Small datasets High parameter efficiency; each layer learns only a few new features Multi-scale lesions Every level of feature is directly reusable Subtle structures Original detail is never lost in transmission Complex texture Strong multi-scale combination Concretely: low-level edge features, mid-level shape features and high-level semantic features are all simultaneously available, gradients flow from shallow layers straight to deep ones, and nothing gets “forgotten” on the way down. Configurations worth starting from Adapting the input layer for a single-channel CT or a multi-modal MR volume is a one-line change: The memory catch Dense connectivity is parameter-efficient but activation-hungry — every intermediate feature map has to be kept for the concatenations. Mitigations: gradient checkpointing (trade compute for memory), smaller batch size, mixed precision, and a well-pipelined data loader. Comparison Model Information flow Feature retention Gradient flow Parameter efficiency Plain CNN Replacement Poor Vanishes easily Medium ResNet Additive fusion Medium Good Good DenseNet Concatenative accumulation Excellent Excellent Excellent What to remember Bottleneck lives inside a block; Transition lives between blocks. Each Dense Block accumulates channels independently; Transition resets the count. Concatenation preserves information, addition mixes it. Growth rate is a hyperparameter you control completely — it is the design knob, not an emergent property.

title.zh: 医学影像深度学习模型全景：CNN、U-Net、Transformer 与基础模型
title.en: Deep Learning Models for Medical Imaging: CNNs, U-Net, Transformers, and Foundation Models

description.zh: 从骨干网络到分割、检测、生成与基础模型——一张医学影像深度学习的全景地图与发展时间线。
description.en: Backbones, segmentation, detection, generative models and foundation models — plus the timeline that connects them.

text.zh: 阅读约 8 分钟 一、 基础与骨干网络（构建模型的基本单元） 这些是构成复杂模型的基石，如同建筑的砖瓦。 模型 核心思想 在医学图像中的作用 CNN 使用卷积核提取局部特征，通过池化层降维。 所有医学图像分析的起点。用于提取图像中的基础特征，如边缘、纹理。 VGG 通过堆叠小的卷积核来增加网络深度。 结构简单，常作为U-Net等分割模型的编码器（主干网络）。 ResNet 引入“残差连接”，解决深层网络梯度消失问题，让网络可以做得非常深。 医学图像中最常用的主干网络。强大的特征提取能力，用于分类、分割和检测。 DenseNet 每一层都与前面所有层相连，特征复用率极高。 作为主干网络，在数据量较小的医学任务中能更高效地利用特征。 EfficientNet 复合缩放网络深度、宽度和分辨率，在计算量和准确率间取得最佳平衡。 适合资源受限（如你的笔记本）的场景，是轻量且高效的主干网络选择。 Vision Transformer 将图像切块，用Transformer的自注意力机制捕捉全局依赖关系。 解决CNN感受野有限的问题，特别适合需要全局信息的任务，如分类、大器官分割。 二、 核心任务模型（解决特定问题的利器） 这些模型直接面向分割、分类、检测等经典任务。 1. 分割模型 模型 核心思想 在医学图像中的作用与优势 U-Net 编码器-解码器 + 跳跃连接。编码器下采样提取特征，解码器上采样恢复空间细节，跳跃连接融合高低层特征。 医学分割的黄金标准。结构对称优雅，特别适合生物医学图像中目标结构复杂、需精确定位的场景。 U-Net++ 在U-Net的编码器和解码器之间构建密集跳跃连接，融合更多不同尺度的特征。 相比U-Net，能提升分割精度，特别是对边界复杂的目标。 Attention U-Net 在跳跃连接处引入注意力门控机制，让网络自动关注目标区域，抑制无关背景。 非常适合在复杂背景中分割小目标（如肿瘤、病灶），能减少假阳性。 V-Net 将U-Net的思想扩展到3D，使用3D卷积，并提出了Dice Loss。 专门为3D医学体积数据（如CT, MRI）设计，能充分利用空间上下文信息。 nnU-Net 一个框架，而非一个新网络。它能根据任何医学分割数据集自动配置包括预处理、网络架构、训练和后处理在内的整个管道。 “无人能及”的医学分割基线。在众多国际挑战赛中夺冠。它证明了鲁棒的管道设计比追求复杂的网络结构更重要。 SETR / Swin-Unet 使用纯Transformer架构（ViT）或分层Transformer（Swin）构建的分割模型。 探索Transformer在分割任务上的潜力，尤其擅长建模长距离依赖，分割大范围结构。 2. 分类与检测模型 模型 核心思想 在医学图像中的作用与优势 EfficientNet/ResNet 用作特征提取器，最后接全连接层进行分类。 图像级别分类的主流方法，如判断一张X光片是否患有肺炎。 Faster R-CNN 两阶段检测器。首先由区域提议网络生成候选框，再对候选框进行分类和精修。 高精度检测，用于精准定位病灶（如肺结节、肿瘤）并给出分类。 YOLO / SSD 单阶段检测器。将检测视为回归问题，直接在网络中预测边界框和类别，速度极快。 实时或高速检测场景，如在手术导航或筛查中快速找出可疑区域。 DETR 使用Transformer直接将目标检测视为一个集合预测问题，无需复杂的锚框和非极大值抑制。 新颖的检测范式，简化了检测 pipeline，避免了NMS等后处理，正在医学检测中展现潜力。 3. 生成与自监督模型 模型 核心思想 在医学图像中的作用与优势 GAN 包含一个生成器和一个判别器，通过“对抗”训练学习数据分布，生成逼真图像。 数据增强（生成罕见病例图像）、图像合成（如MRI生成CT）、图像去噪、超分辨率重建。 Diffusion Model 通过一个“加噪”和“去噪”的过程学习数据分布，是目前最强的生成模型。 同样用于图像生成和增强，生成的图像细节更丰富、更逼真，正在超越GAN。 MAE / SimCLR 自监督学习。通过设计预任务（如图像掩码重建、图像对比学习）从无标签数据中学习通用特征表示。 解决医学数据标注昂贵的问题。先在海量无标签医学图像上预训练，再用少量标注数据微调，可大幅提升模型性能。 三、 医学基础模型（Foundation Models） 这是当前最前沿的方向，旨在构建能解决多种任务的通用医学AI。 模型类型 核心思想 代表模型/方法 在医学图像中的作用与优势 通用视觉模型 在超大规模通用图像-文本对（如LAION）上训练。 CLIP 通过提示学习实现零样本分类，但直接用于医学领域存在领域差距。 专用基础模型 在大规模、多模态医学数据（图像+报告文本）上预训练。 Med-PaLM M, LVM, “慧影” 真正为医学领域定制。能理解医学概念，通过微调或提示执行分类、分割、检测、问答等多种任务，泛化能力强。 如何系统地学习和应用？ 从U-Net和ResNet开始：彻底理解它们的代码和思想。这是你的“基石”。 掌握nnU-Net：学习它的设计哲学和代码实现。它会教你如何构建一个鲁棒、自动化的医学图像分割系统，这比单纯学一个新网络更有价值。 根据任务选择模型： 精细分割：尝试Attention U-Net, U-Net++。 3D数据：使用V-Net或3D nnU-Net。 资源受限：选择EfficientNet作为主干。 数据量少：探索自监督学习（MAE）或使用预训练的基础模型进行微调。 需要全局上下文：尝试Vision Transformer或Swin Transformer。 关注前沿：持续跟踪MICCAI、CVPR等顶会论文，了解Diffusion Model和医学基础模型的最新进展。 医学影像分析模型发展时间线 第一阶段：深度学习黎明前的黑暗（2012年以前） 技术背景：传统机器学习方法主导，依赖手工设计特征（如SIFT、HOG） + 分类器（如SVM）。 在医学影像中的应用：主要用于图像配准、分割（如水平集、图割）和初步分类，性能遇到瓶颈。 第二阶段：CNN的崛起与初步应用（2012-2014） 核心思想：让网络自动从数据中学习层次化特征。 里程碑模型： AlexNet (2012) 意义：开创了深度CNN在图像识别领域的胜利，点燃了深度学习的热潮。 医学影响：研究者开始尝试将AlexNet及其思想迁移到医学任务中，证明了深度学习在医学影像上的潜力。 ZFNet (2013) & VGGNet (2014) 意义：通过可视化（ZFNet）和更深的网络结构（VGG），深化了对CNN工作原理的理解，并证明了“深度”的重要性。 医学影响：VGG的规整结构成为许多早期医学影像研究项目的基础骨干网络。 第三阶段：网络深度与结构的革命（2015-2016） 核心问题：如何训练更深的网络？如何提升信息流动？ 里程碑模型： U-Net (2015) 意义：医学影像分割的里程碑。提出了经典的编码器-解码器结构和跳跃连接，完美解决了医学图像像素级定位的需求。 医学影响：至今仍是医学图像分割的黄金标准和基线模型，催生了无数变体。 ResNet (2015) 意义：提出残差连接（Skip Connection），解决了深度网络的梯度消失/爆炸问题，使得训练数百甚至上千层的网络成为可能。 医学影响：取代VGG成为更强大的特征提取骨干网络，用于分类、检测等任务。 DenseNet (2016) 意义：将残差连接的思想推向极致，提出了密集连接，促进了特征复用，大幅减少了参数量。 医学影响：在数据量较小的医学任务中，其高效的特征提取能力备受青睐。 第四阶段：注意力机制与高效化（2017-2019） 核心问题：如何让网络更“专注”？如何在精度和效率间取得平衡？ 里程碑模型： 注意力机制系列 (2017-) SE-Net (2017)：通道注意力，让网络关注“什么是重要的通道”。 CBAM (2018)：同时结合通道和空间注意力。 医学影响：成为提升各类CNN骨干网络（ResNet, DenseNet）性能的即插即用模块，尤其适合聚焦于微小病变。 EfficientNet (2019) 意义：提出复合模型缩放方法，系统性地平衡网络的深度、宽度和分辨率，在同等算力下达到最优性能。 医学影响：为资源受限的临床环境（如移动端、边缘计算）提供了高效的模型选择。 第五阶段：Transformer的跨界与冲击（2020-2021） 核心思想：用自注意力（Self-Attention）机制完全替代或增强卷积，捕捉全局依赖关系。 里程碑模型： Vision Transformer (ViT) (2020) 意义：证明了纯Transformer结构在计算机视觉任务上的卓越能力，尤其是在大数据预训练下。 医学影响：开启了医学影像分析的“Transformer时代”。 Swin Transformer (2021) 意义：引入了移位窗口和分层设计，使Transformer能像CNN一样高效处理多尺度特征，并降低了计算复杂度。 医学影响：迅速成为新一代强大的通用视觉骨干网络。 UNETR / TransUNet (2021) 意义：CNN-Transformer混合架构的典范。用Transformer作为编码器捕捉全局上下文，用CNN（或Transformer）解码器进行精确定位。 医学影响：在多个医学分割公开数据集上达到SOTA，成为U-Net最有力的竞争者。 第六阶段：专用化、自动化与生成模型（2022至今） 核心趋势：模型设计更加专业化、自动化，并利用生成模型解决数据稀缺等问题。 前沿模型/技术： nnU-Net (2020，但影响持续) 意义：“无脑”使用的自动化管道。它不提出新的网络结构，而是通过自动配置数据预处理、网络拓扑、训练策略等，在多种分割任务上取得惊人效果。 医学影响：证明了在医学领域，鲁棒的工程管道与新颖的架构同等重要。 ConvNeXt (2022) 意义：“现代化”的CNN。通过借鉴Transformer的一些设计理念（如大卷积核），让纯CNN的性能反超了Swin Transformer。 医学影响：为社区提供了除Transformer外的另一个强大选择，特别适合希望保持CNN结构简洁性的场景。 扩散模型 (2022-) 意义：新一代生成模型，在图像生成、超分辨率、去噪和异常检测方面展现出巨大潜力。 医学影响：用于数据增强（生成合成医学图像）、图像重建（从低剂量CT生成高清图像）和异常检测。
text.en: 14 min read An attempt to organise the model landscape in medical image analysis into something I could navigate, rather than a list of names I half-recognised. 1. Backbones — the building blocks These are the bricks that more complex models are made from. Model Core idea Role in medical imaging CNN Convolution extracts local features; pooling reduces dimension The starting point for everything. Extracts basic features such as edges and texture VGG Depth through stacked small kernels Simple structure; often the encoder backbone for U-Net and similar ResNet Residual connections solve vanishing gradients in deep networks The most common backbone. Strong features for classification, segmentation and detection DenseNet Every layer connects to all previous layers; very high feature reuse Efficient with limited data, which suits many medical tasks EfficientNet Compound scaling of depth, width and resolution Good where compute is constrained; light and efficient Vision Transformer Patch the image, use self-attention for global dependency Fixes the CNN’s limited receptive field; suits tasks needing global context 2. Task-specific models Segmentation Model Core idea Why it matters here U-Net Encoder–decoder with skip connections The gold standard for medical segmentation. Symmetric, elegant, precise where structures are complex U-Net++ Dense skip connections between encoder and decoder Better accuracy than U-Net, especially on complex boundaries Attention U-Net Attention gates on the skip connections Good for small targets in cluttered backgrounds; reduces false positives V-Net U-Net extended to 3D, introduces Dice loss Built for 3D volumes such as CT and MRI nnU-Net A framework, not a network — auto-configures the whole pipeline The benchmark that keeps winning challenges. Proof that a robust pipeline beats a clever architecture SETR / Swin-Unet Pure or hierarchical Transformer segmentation Explores long-range dependency for large structures Classification and detection Model Core idea Use EfficientNet / ResNet Feature extractor plus a dense head Image-level classification, e.g. pneumonia on a chest X-ray Faster R-CNN Two-stage: propose regions, then classify and refine High-precision lesion localisation YOLO / SSD Single-stage regression, very fast Real-time screening or surgical navigation DETR Transformer treats detection as set prediction Removes anchors and NMS; simplifies the pipeline Generative and self-supervised Model Core idea Use GAN Generator and discriminator trained adversarially Data augmentation for rare cases, modality synthesis, denoising, super-resolution Diffusion models Learn the distribution through noising and denoising Richer detail than GANs; generation, reconstruction, anomaly detection MAE / SimCLR Self-supervised pretext tasks on unlabelled data Addresses the cost of medical annotation — pretrain on unlabelled scans, fine-tune on few labels 3. Foundation models Type Core idea Examples Why it matters General vision Trained on huge general image–text pairs CLIP Zero-shot classification via prompting, but a real domain gap in medicine Domain-specific Pretrained on large multimodal medical data — images plus reports Med-PaLM M, LVM Genuinely built for the domain; generalises across classification, segmentation, detection and QA How to actually learn this The nnU-Net point is the one that changed how I think: it proposes no new architecture at all, and still wins. Robust engineering of preprocessing, topology, training strategy and postprocessing turned out to matter more than a novel module. Timeline Before 2012 — before deep learning Classical machine learning dominated: hand-designed features such as SIFT and HOG, feeding a classifier such as an SVM. In medical imaging this meant registration, level-set or graph-cut segmentation, and basic classification — all hitting a ceiling. 2012–2014 — CNNs arrive AlexNet (2012) — the first decisive win for deep CNNs in image recognition. Researchers immediately began transferring the idea to medical tasks. ZFNet (2013) and VGGNet (2014) — visualisation deepened understanding of what CNNs do; depth was shown to matter. VGG’s regular structure became the backbone for many early medical studies. 2015–2016 — depth and structure U-Net (2015) — the landmark for medical segmentation. Encoder–decoder plus skip connections solved pixel-level localisation. Still the baseline today. ResNet (2015) — residual connections made very deep networks trainable, and replaced VGG as the standard backbone. DenseNet (2016) — pushed the idea further with dense connectivity, improving feature reuse and cutting parameters. Popular where data is scarce. 2017–2019 — attention and efficiency SE-Net (2017) — channel attention: which channels matter. CBAM (2018) — channel and spatial attention together. EfficientNet (2019) — compound scaling for the best accuracy at a given compute budget. Attention blocks became plug-in upgrades for existing backbones, particularly useful for focusing on small lesions. 2020–2021 — the Transformer arrives ViT (2020) — pure Transformers work for vision, given enough pretraining data. Swin Transformer (2021) — shifted windows and hierarchical design brought multi-scale efficiency, and it quickly became a general-purpose backbone. UNETR / TransUNet (2021) — hybrid CNN–Transformer segmentation; state of the art on several public datasets and U-Net’s most serious competition. 2022 onwards — specialisation, automation, generation nnU-Net — automated configuration proved that pipeline robustness rivals architectural novelty. ConvNeXt (2022) — a “modernised” CNN borrowing Transformer design ideas, overtaking Swin. A reminder that CNNs were not finished. Diffusion models (2022–) — augmentation, reconstruction from low-dose CT, and anomaly detection. What the map is for Writing this did not make me an expert on any single row. What it gave me was the ability to place a new paper: when MM-UNet appeared, I could immediately see it as a U-Net descendant that swaps the Transformer bottleneck for Mamba, for exactly the efficiency reason the 2020–2021 row created.

title.zh: MM-UNet MACM 模块详解：多尺度各向异性卷积如何提取 3D 特征
title.en: MM-UNet MACM Explained: Multi-Scale Anisotropic Convolutions for 3D Features

description.zh: 用四个尺度的各向异性卷积分支，同时理解切片内结构与切片间连续性，并控制大卷积核的成本。
description.en: Splitting k×k×k into orthogonal branches cuts roughly 84% of the parameters and fits MR's uneven slice spacing.

text.zh: 阅读约 7 分钟 专题：MM-UNet 论文精读。前置知识：参数量计算、GFLOPs 计算、U-Net 结构详解。相关章节：AFFM、GCM。 3D MRI 并不是由完全等距的立方体组成。前列腺 MR 常见的情况是：切片平面内分辨率较高，切片之间的间距却更大。MACM 因此不使用一个各方向完全相同的立方卷积核，而是把平面内信息与跨切片信息分开处理。 模块先做多尺度，再做融合 这不是把原输入与多尺度结果做一次简单残差相加。论文描述的是把输入与四个 ACB 分支的结果连接起来，再用 1×1×1 卷积完成融合与通道整理。这样，每个尺度的信息都被显式保留下来。 小卷积核偏向局部边缘和纹理，大卷积核覆盖更宽的器官形状与邻近结构。四个尺度同时存在，是为了避免只用一个固定感受野来解释大小和形态会变化的前列腺。 一个 ACB 里有两个方向 1×1×k：跨切片 这一支只沿深度轴展开，重点观察相邻切片之间的连续变化。它帮助网络追踪前列腺从底部到顶部时形状如何改变，也能减少相邻切片预测边界忽然跳动的问题。 k×k×1：切片内 这一支在单张切片的平面上扩大感受野，关注局部纹理、轮廓以及前列腺与周围组织的关系。深度方向保持为 1，因此不会把粗糙的层间分辨率当成与平面内完全相同。 两条支路输出尺寸一致，所以可以相加。这里的“各向异性”不是一个装饰性名词，而是把 MRI 三个方向不同的物理间距直接反映到卷积核形状中。 为什么大卷积核还可以接受 直接使用 k×k×k 卷积时，单个输入—输出通道对需要 k³ 个权重。把不同方向拆开后，成本可以显著降低。 形式 核的结构 单通道参数量的量级 标准 3D 卷积 k×k×k k³ 各向异性双分支 1×1×k 与 k×k×1 k + k² 三轴分解 k×1×1、1×k×1、1×1×k 3k 论文还讨论了把大 3D 卷积分解为沿三个轴的卷积组合。要注意：3k 是这种三轴分解的参数量，不应直接拿来描述上面 ACB 的两条并行分支。把这两件事分开，计算逻辑才不会混乱。 MACM 在 MM-UNet 里做什么 AFFM 先筛选并融合编码器细节与解码器语义；MACM 随后在多个尺度上整理这份融合特征，让它同时满足两种需求：在切片内精确定位边界，在切片之间保持三维连续性。 我会用下面的顺序记住它： 用 1×1×1 卷积控制通道。 把同一输入送入四个不同尺度的 ACB。 每个 ACB 再把平面内与跨切片信息分开建模。 拼接原输入与四个尺度的输出。 用最后的 1×1×1 卷积完成融合。 MACM 的核心不是“卷积核越大越好”，而是让卷积核的方向与尺度都对应真实的体数据几何。 资料来源：A mixed Mamba U-net for prostate segmentation in MR images
text.en: 7 min read Series: MM-UNet paper notes. Background: parameter count, GFLOPs, U-Net explained. Related chapters: AFFM, GCM. Notes on MM-UNet’s Multi-scale Anisotropic Convolution Module — a feature extractor designed specifically for 3D medical volumes. What it is for MACM targets three problems at once: Anisotropic resolution — spacing differs between axes. Multi-scale demand — local detail and global context both matter. Computational cost — performance cannot come at any price. Structure A 1×1×1 convolution sets the channel count. Four anisotropic convolution blocks process the features in parallel at different scales. The adjusted input and the four branch outputs are concatenated along the channel axis. A final 1×1×1 convolution fuses the result and sets the output channels. Inside an ACB Branch one — 1×1×k, across slices Handles relationships along the z axis: continuity between consecutive slices, and three-dimensional context within the volume. In prostate segmentation this is what tracks the gland’s changing shape from base to apex, follows the urethra through multiple slices, and keeps the boundary consistent from one slice to the next. Branch two — k×k×1, within the plane Handles spatial patterns inside a single slice: texture, boundary contour, local anatomical structure. This is what detects the gland outline precisely, distinguishes internal tissue heterogeneity, and picks up local features such as cysts and calcifications. Combining them $$F_{\text{ACB}} = F_{\text{slice}} + F_{\text{plane}}$$ Addition is cheap, adds no parameters, and lets gradients flow cleanly through both branches. The cost argument A standard 3D convolution has O(k³) parameters, growing cubically with kernel size. MACM factorises it into a 1×1×k and a k×k×1 branch. Kernel type Parameters At k = 7 Standard 3D k³ 343 Factorised ACB k + k² 56 Reduction 1 − (k + k²) / k³ 84% $$\text{reduction} = 1 - \frac{k + k^2}{k^3} = 1 - \left( \frac{1}{k^2} + \frac{1}{k} \right)$$ The factorisation works because feature space is approximately separable, directional information is relatively independent, and medical images are structurally regular enough for that assumption to hold. Why four different kernel sizes Kernel Receptive field Main role Where it helps k = 3 Local Fine detail Precise boundary placement k = 7 Medium Structural features Internal tissue analysis k = 13 Large Context modelling Relationships between organs k = 15 Global Whole-shape context Overall morphology Running them in parallel means the scale coverage is complete — from pixel-level detail to organ-level structure — and the module stays robust when target size varies. Fit to prostate MR specifically In-plane resolution is roughly 0.5–1.0 mm; slice thickness is 3–5 mm. The ACB split matches that asymmetry directly rather than pretending the voxels are cubes. Small kernel (k = 3) — detects subtle boundary changes, identifies cysts and small calcifications. Medium kernel (k = 7) — analyses internal gland structure, separates the central zone from the peripheral zone. Large kernels (k = 13, 15) — capture the spatial relationship with bladder and rectum, and the overall shape and position. The thing I found most instructive: the module’s design is not a general improvement borrowed from elsewhere. Every choice in it is traceable back to a physical property of the scanner output.

title.zh: MM-UNet GCM 模块详解：Mamba 如何建模 3D MRI 全局上下文
title.en: MM-UNet GCM Explained: Modeling Global Context in 3D MRI with Mamba

description.zh: 把 3D 特征体展开为序列，在保留卷积局部能力的同时，用 Mamba 以线性复杂度建模长距离联系。
description.en: Flatten the volume into a sequence and get long-range dependency at linear cost instead of quadratic.

text.zh: 阅读约 7 分钟 专题：MM-UNet 论文精读。前置知识：注意力与 Transformer 基础、GFLOPs 计算。相关章节：整体架构、AFFM、MACM。 GCM 是 MM-UNet 的瓶颈模块。它先用卷积整理局部特征，再把三维空间展开成序列交给 Mamba，最后恢复原来的空间形状。它回答的问题不是“边缘在哪里”，而是“相距很远的区域如何共同构成一个完整器官”。 整体结构 这里 $L = H \times W \times D$。空间中的每个位置都成为序列中的一个元素，而通道维 C 继续描述这个位置包含什么特征。 为什么先经过两个残差块 卷积擅长局部纹理和边界，Mamba 擅长长距离联系。GCM 没有让后者替代前者，而是先把局部表示整理好，再做全局建模。残差连接让模块学习对输入的修正，也为梯度保留了一条短路径。 Mamba 块里的两条分支 内容分支负责混合局部与长距离信息，状态空间层会把此前位置的摘要带到当前位置。 门控分支决定哪些响应应该通过。 两条分支做逐元素乘法后再投影回输出维度，因此门控是在调节内容，而不是生成另一份独立结果。 选择性状态空间在更新什么 最值得记住的是状态 h。它不是最终预测，而是序列进行到当前位置时的内部记忆。输出 y_t 与下一步要继续携带的 h_t 都由本次更新得到，因此不能把二者画成同一条先后链。 选择性来自参数会随当前输入改变：有用信息可以被写入状态，无关信息可以被压低。这样，全局关系不需要像自注意力那样让每个位置与所有位置两两比较。 它在 MM-UNet 中的位置 GCM 放在分辨率最低、语义最浓缩的瓶颈处。此时序列长度比在原图上更短，既能看到全局，也能控制计算成本。它输出的形状与输入一致，所以可以接回原本的 U-Net 解码路径。 我会怎样检查自己的理解 输入和输出是否保持同一个五维形状。 展平只改变组织方式，没有丢掉空间位置对应关系。 卷积残差块负责局部精炼，Mamba 负责长程依赖，两者职责不同。 门控分支与内容分支在逐元素乘法处汇合。 状态 h_t 被传向下一位置，输出 y_t 则服务于当前序列表示。 GCM 的重点不是“使用了一个新模块”，而是把卷积的局部归纳偏置与状态空间模型的全局效率放在了合适的位置。 资料来源：A mixed Mamba U-net for prostate segmentation in MR images
text.en: 8 min read Series: MM-UNet paper notes. Background: attention and Transformer basics, GFLOPs. Related chapters: the overall architecture, AFFM, MACM. Detailed notes on MM-UNet’s Global Context-aware Module. It combines a CNN’s local feature extraction with Mamba’s long-sequence modelling to capture global context efficiently. Overall structure GCM takes a 5D input: batch, channels, height, width, depth. Two residual blocks refine local features first. The spatial map is flattened into a sequence so Mamba can process it. After layer norm, the Mamba block models global context. The sequence is reshaped back into spatial form. The residual block The skip connection means the block learns a correction rather than a full transformation, which keeps gradients healthy. Inside the Mamba block Branch one produces the content and builds long-range dependency. Branch two produces importance weights — a judgement about how reliable each feature is. They are combined element-wise, so the output carries both the content and an assessment of it. The selective state-space mechanism Four properties worth remembering: Dynamic parameterisation. Δ, B and C are computed from the current input rather than being fixed. Selectivity. Because those parameters depend on the input, the model can choose what to retain and what to ignore. State passing. A state vector h accumulates history, which is how global information travels. Hardware friendliness. Training parallelises; inference runs as an efficient recurrence. Where it sits in the pipeline The encoder finds edges and texture; GCM establishes how the parts relate to each other as an organ; the decoder combines both to place the boundary. Why it helps Global context — long-range spatial dependency becomes representable. Linear complexity — feasible on 3D volumes, unlike quadratic attention. Selective attention — important features are amplified, noise suppressed. Drop-in — it slots into an existing U-Net without redesigning the architecture. Stable training — residual connections keep gradients flowing. Specifications Input and output — the same 5D shape, $B \times C \times H \times W \times D$. Sequence length — $L = H \times W \times D$. Expansion — 2L, giving each branch its own working space. Activations — HardSwish inside Mamba, LeakyReLU in the residual blocks. Normalisation — instance norm in the residual blocks, layer norm before Mamba.

title.zh: MM-UNet AFFM 模块详解：自适应特征融合如何抑制背景噪声
title.en: MM-UNet AFFM Explained: Adaptive Feature Fusion for Suppressing Background Noise

description.zh: 自适应特征融合模块用通道注意力筛选低层细节，再与已经对齐的高层语义特征相加。
description.en: A learned weight per channel, so detail gets through without dragging the background noise along with it.

text.zh: 阅读约 6 分钟 专题：MM-UNet 论文精读。前置知识：SENet 通道注意力、U-Net 结构详解。相关章节：整体架构、MACM。 U-Net 的跳跃连接要把编码器的低层细节送给解码器，但“细节丰富”与“噪声很多”常常同时发生。AFFM 的思路是：不要直接融合，先根据高低层特征共同产生一组通道权重，再决定哪些低层信息值得保留。 两类特征各自带来什么 特征 优点 风险 编码器低层特征 边缘、纹理与精确位置 背景噪声多，缺少整体语义 解码器高层特征 器官轮廓与类别语义 空间分辨率低，边界较粗 AFFM 不是在两者中二选一，而是让高层语义帮助判断低层通道是否有用。 完整信息流 这张图里最容易画错的是最后一条旁路：参与相加的高层特征已经完成上采样，否则它与低层特征的空间尺寸不一致。 第一步：对齐并拼接 $$F_c = \mathrm{concat}\bigl( F_{\text{low}},\ \mathrm{upsample}(F_{\text{high}}) \bigr)$$ 上采样只负责把高层特征恢复到同一空间尺度；拼接得到的 F_c 同时包含局部细节与高层语义，它的任务是为后面的通道权重提供判断依据。 第二步：计算通道权重 $$\alpha = \sigma\Bigl( W_2 \ \mathrm{ReLU}\bigl( W_1 \ \mathrm{GAP}(F_c) \bigr) \Bigr)$$ 全局平均池化把每个通道压缩成一个数，概括该通道在整个特征图上的响应。 两个全连接层学习通道之间的依赖关系。 Sigmoid 把结果限制在 0 到 1 之间。 α 接近 1，表示该通道对当前分割更有用；接近 0，则意味着它更可能是背景干扰。这里的权重来自数据与任务，而不是人工阈值。 第三步：重标定并融合 $$\text{output} = \alpha \odot F_{\text{low}} + \mathrm{upsample}(F_{\text{high}})$$ 论文中的权重作用在低层特征上，因为低层分支同时包含细节与噪声，更需要筛选。高层分支主要承担语义引导，并在尺寸对齐后直接参与相加。 使用加法而不是再次拼接有两个好处：不会继续扩大通道数，也不需要额外卷积来压回原维度。但这也意味着两条分支在相加前必须具有兼容的空间大小与通道数。 它在跳跃连接中的作用 传统跳跃连接像把整张细节图直接递给解码器；AFFM 更像在交接前做一次编辑：保留边界与纹理，把与前列腺无关的背景响应压低。随后 MACM 再从不同尺度和方向整理这些融合特征。 我会用四个问题检查实现： 高层特征是否先被上采样到匹配尺寸。 权重是否由拼接后的高低层信息共同产生。 alpha 是否只重标定低层特征。 最终相加的两条分支是否已经完成尺寸与通道对齐。 AFFM 的价值不在于“多了一层注意力”，而在于它把筛选放在噪声进入解码器之前。 资料来源：A mixed Mamba U-net for prostate segmentation in MR images
text.en: 5 min read Series: MM-UNet paper notes. Background: SENet channel attention, U-Net explained. Related chapters: the overall architecture, MACM. Detailed notes on MM-UNet’s Adaptive Feature Fusion Module. The problem it addresses The conventional skip connection concatenates high-level and low-level features directly. That means: Background noise from the shallow layers mixes into genuinely useful information. The final boundary becomes less precise, not more. Two maps, two characters AFFM behaves like a careful cartographer merging two maps. Low-level features High-level features Think of it as A detail map An outline map Strength Rich edges and texture Knows the overall shape of the prostate Weakness Heavy background noise, no global sense No precise localisation How it works, in three steps Step one — align and concatenate $$F_c = \mathrm{concat}\bigl( \mathrm{upsample}(F_{\text{high}}),\ F_{\text{low}} \bigr)$$ Upsampling brings the high-level map to the same spatial size, so the two can be combined at one scale. Step two — compute the weights $$\alpha = \sigma\Bigl( W_2 \ W_1 \ \mathrm{GAP}(F_c) \Bigr)$$ Global average pooling reduces each channel to a single number — a summary of how strongly that channel responded overall. Two fully connected layers learn the relationships between channels. Sigmoid squashes the result into 0–1. $\alpha \approx 1$ means keep this channel. $\alpha \approx 0$ means suppress it. Step three — weighted fusion $$\text{output} = \alpha \odot F_{\text{low}} + \mathrm{upsample}(F_{\text{high}})$$ Two design choices worth pausing on: Why weight only the low-level features? They are the mixed bag — full of both useful edges and noise, so they are what needs filtering. The high-level features are already comparatively clean and carry the semantic meaning; reweighting them risks distorting information the network worked hard to build. Why add instead of concatenate? Addition is cheaper, introduces no extra parameters, and combines the two signals naturally. Concatenation would grow the channel count and require another convolution to reduce it again. Why it is a good module Noise suppression is learned, not specified. Nobody writes a rule for which channels are noisy; the network works it out. Selection rather than accumulation. It is not “use everything and hope”, it is “decide, then use”. Trained end to end. The attention weights are optimised by the same loss as everything else. Where it sits in MM-UNet AFFM runs at every decoder stage, right after upsampling: Applied layer by layer, this keeps fine detail available in the early stages while letting deep semantics fill in the global picture — which is what precise boundary localisation actually needs. The one-line version AFFM is not feature concatenation with extra steps. It is the network learning what to look at before it looks — and cleaning only the input that needs cleaning, while leaving the already-good input alone.

title.zh: MM-UNet 论文详解：3D MRI 分割架构与 AFFM、GCM、MACM 模块
title.en: MM-UNet Explained: 3D MRI Segmentation with AFFM, GCM, and MACM

description.zh: MM-UNet 的三个创新点：AFFM 如何过滤噪声、GCM 如何看见全局、MACM 如何适应各向异性分辨率。
description.en: Three modules answering three problems — noisy feature fusion, missing global context, and anisotropic resolution.

text.zh: 阅读约 5 分钟 专题：MM-UNet 论文精读。前置知识：U-Net 结构详解、SENet 通道注意力、研究背景。相关章节：Res2Net 编码器、AFFM、GCM、MACM。 核心目标：为什么要做这个研究？ 医生有一张前列腺的3D核磁共振（MR）图像，他们需要精确地知道图像中哪些像素是属于前列腺的。这个过程叫做”分割”。 手动分割的问题：非常耗时、费力，而且不同医生的判断可能会有差异。 自动分割的挑战：计算机来做这件事，面临三个主要难题： 图像质量差：MR图像背景杂乱（噪声多），前列腺边界模糊。 关系复杂：前列腺的形状和它周围的组织（膀胱、直肠等）是相互关联的，计算机需要理解整个图像的”上下文”才能准确判断边界。 数据特殊：3D的MR图像在上下、左右、前后三个方向的分辨率（清晰度）是不一样的。这导致传统的3D处理方法效果不好。 MM-UNet 就是为了解决这三个挑战而设计的。 整体信息流 图里的 AFFM 与 MACM 不是只在网络末端执行一次，它们参与逐级跳跃连接与解码。这样画，是为了先把一轮完整的信息交换说清楚。 创新点一：自适应特征融合模块 (AFFM) – 解决”如何精准融合信息” 1. 为什么需要它？ 在分割网络中，存在两种信息： 低级特征：来自网络的浅层，包含丰富的细节信息（如边缘、纹理），但也混有很多背景噪声。 高级特征：来自网络的深层，包含抽象的语义信息（知道”这是前列腺”），但缺乏细节，比较粗糙。 传统方法简单地把这两种特征拼接在一起，相当于把一张清晰的细节图（带噪点）和一张模糊的轮廓图直接叠在一起。噪声会干扰最终的结果。 2. 它是怎么做到的？ AFFM的核心思想是：在融合之前，先计算一个”重要性权重”，告诉网络哪些特征该保留，哪些该抑制。 它的工作步骤非常明确： 输入：接收来自解码器的高级特征和来自编码器的对应低级特征。 对齐：将高级特征进行上采样，使其尺寸与低级特征相同。 拼接：将对齐后的高级特征和低级特征在通道维度上拼接起来。 计算权重： 全局平均池化：对每个特征通道，计算其所有像素值的平均值。这个平均值代表了该通道的”全局重要性”。 全连接层 + Sigmoid：将这个平均值输入一个小型神经网络（通常是两个全连接层），最后通过Sigmoid函数，为每一个特征通道生成一个0到1之间的权重值。 权重接近1：说明这个通道的特征对分割前列腺非常有用，要保留。 权重接近0：说明这个通道的特征多是噪声或无用的，要抑制。 重标定：把通道权重作用在噪声更复杂的低层特征上。 融合：将加权后的低层特征与已经上采样对齐的高层特征相加。 简单总结：AFFM就像一个智能滤波器，在融合高低层信息时，自动放大有用的信号，减弱无用的噪声。 创新点二：全局上下文感知模块 (GCM) – 解决”如何理解全局关系” 1. 为什么需要它？ 传统的卷积神经网络（CNN）一次只能看到图像的一个小局部（感受野有限）。它很难理解”前列腺的顶部和底部在形态上是如何呼应的”这种长距离依赖关系。 Transformer模型虽然能捕捉全局信息，但其计算量随着图像尺寸的增大会呈平方级增长。对于3D医学图像（尺寸很大），这会导致计算非常缓慢，内存消耗巨大。 2. 它是怎么做到的？ GCM引入了名为Mamba的新模型来解决这个问题。Mamba的核心优势是：它能以线性复杂度（计算量随尺寸匀速增长）来处理序列信息，并捕捉长距离依赖。 它的工作步骤： 输入：接收编码器输出的最底层、最抽象的特征图（尺寸最小，如16x16x16）。 预处理：先用几个标准的卷积层（残差块）对特征进行初步优化。 序列化：将3D特征图（B, C, H, W, D）展平并转换成一个序列（B, L, C）。这里，L = H * W * D，就是把3D空间中的每一个点都看作是序列里的一个”单词”。 Mamba处理：将这个序列输入Mamba块。 Mamba内部有一套称为状态空间模型（SSM）的机制，可以理解为它有一个”记忆系统”。当它处理序列中的每一个”单词”时，会参考之前所有”单词”的信息，从而建立起全局理解。 关键在于，Mamba通过数学上的优化，使得这个”记忆和参考”的过程计算效率非常高，远低于Transformer。 恢复形状：将Mamba处理后的序列再重新转换回3D特征图的格式（B, C, H, W, D）。 输出：输出一个既包含局部细节，又蕴含了全局上下文信息的、增强后的特征图。 简单总结：GCM利用高效的Mamba模型，让网络在瓶颈处能”纵观全局”，理解整个前列腺的结构关系，弥补了CNN”只看局部”的缺陷。 创新点三：多尺度各向异性卷积模块 (MACM) – 解决”如何适应不均匀分辨率” 1. 为什么需要它？ 前列腺MR图像是各向异性的。通常，在横断面（左右、前后）分辨率高（如0.5mm），但在上下方向分辨率低（如3.0mm）。 使用标准的3x3x3卷积核去处理这种数据，就像用一个大正方体去量一个扁盒子，无法精确捕捉其真实形状，而且计算量大。 2. 它是怎么做到的？ MACM采用了两大策略：”多尺度”和”卷积分解”。 策略一：并行多尺度 模块内部并行设置了多个不同大小的卷积核（例如3, 7, 13, 15）。 小卷积核（如3）：负责捕捉细微的边缘和纹理。 大卷积核（如15）：负责捕捉更大范围的形态和结构。 最后将所有分支提取的特征拼接起来，这样网络就能同时看到”树木”和”森林”。 策略二：3D卷积分解 这是为了高效处理各向异性。 传统3D卷积（如k x k x k）的参数是k³。 MACM将其分解为三个连续的1D卷积： 一个k x 1 x 1的卷积，只处理上下方向。 一个1 x k x 1的卷积，只处理左右方向。 一个1 x 1 x k的卷积，只处理前后方向。 好处： 参数量大幅减少：从k³降为3k。以k=7为例，参数量从343降为21，减少了约94%！ 适配各向异性：网络可以独立地在三个不同方向上学习特征，更好地适应MR图像分辨率不均的特点。 简单总结：MACM通过使用多种”尺子”和把大尺子拆成三把小尺子的方法，既高效又精准地提取了3D各向异性图像的特征。 总结：MM-UNet如何工作 整个模型就是一个精心设计的U型管道： 编码器（下采样）：使用3D Res2Net，像剥洋葱一样，一层层提取图像特征，从细节到轮廓。 瓶颈层：在管道最窄处，GCM登场，为这些特征注入全局理解。 解码器（上采样）：一步步恢复图像分辨率。 每一步，AFFM负责智能地融合来自编码器的细节和当前的特征。 融合后，MACM负责进一步优化这个融合后的特征，使其适应3D各向异性。 输出：最后通过一个简单的卷积层，为每个像素计算属于前列腺的概率，生成最终的分割图。
text.en: 9 min read Series: MM-UNet paper notes. Background: U-Net explained, SENet channel attention, the research background. Related chapters: the Res2Net encoder, AFFM, GCM, MACM. Notes on A mixed Mamba U-net for prostate segmentation in MR images. This is the overview; the three modules each get their own note afterwards. What the paper is trying to do A radiologist has a 3D prostate MR volume and needs to know exactly which voxels belong to the prostate. Doing it by hand is slow, tiring, and inconsistent between readers. Automating it runs into three difficulties: Image quality. MR volumes are noisy and the prostate boundary is often genuinely blurred. Contextual relationships. The prostate’s shape is entangled with the bladder and rectum around it, so a correct boundary depends on understanding the whole scene. Anisotropy. Resolution differs by axis — fine in-plane, coarse between slices — which breaks methods that assume isotropic voxels. MM-UNet proposes one module per difficulty. The pipeline Module one — AFFM, for fusing without importing noise A segmentation network carries two kinds of information: Low-level features from shallow layers: rich in edges and texture, but also full of background noise. High-level features from deep layers: they know this is prostate, but they are spatially coarse. The conventional move is to concatenate them, which is equivalent to laying a sharp but noisy detail map over a blurred outline and hoping for the best. The noise comes along for the ride. AFFM computes an importance weight before fusing: Take the decoder’s high-level features and the encoder’s matching low-level features. Upsample the high-level features to the same size. Concatenate along the channel axis. Global average pooling gives one number per channel — a summary of that channel’s overall response. Two fully connected layers and a sigmoid turn those into weights in 0–1. Multiply, then fuse. A weight near 1 means this channel is useful, keep it. Near 0 means this is mostly noise, suppress it. It is an attention mechanism acting as a learned filter rather than a fixed rule. Module two — GCM, for seeing the whole organ CNNs have a bounded receptive field, so a relationship between the apex and the base of the prostate is hard to represent. Transformers can represent it but cost O(n²), which is punishing on a 3D volume. GCM uses Mamba instead, which models sequences in linear time. Take the smallest, most abstract feature map from the encoder bottleneck. Refine it with a couple of residual convolution blocks. Flatten the 3D map (B, C, H, W, D) into a sequence (B, L, C) where $L = H \times W \times D$ — every spatial position becomes one token. Run it through a Mamba block. Its state-space mechanism carries a running summary of everything seen so far, which is what builds global understanding. Reshape back to 3D. The output holds both local detail and global context, at a cost that grows linearly rather than quadratically with volume size. Module three — MACM, for uneven resolution Prostate MR is typically ~0.5 mm in-plane and ~3.0 mm between slices. Using a standard 3×3×3 kernel on that data is like measuring a flat box with a cube — it neither fits the shape nor spends compute sensibly. MACM applies two ideas at once. Parallel multi-scale. Several kernel sizes run side by side — 3, 7, 13, 15. Small kernels catch fine edges and texture; large kernels catch overall shape and the organ’s relationship to its neighbours. Their outputs are concatenated, so the network sees both the trees and the forest. Factorised 3D convolution. Instead of one k×k×k kernel, use three consecutive 1D convolutions, one per axis. Kernel type Parameters At k = 7 Standard 3D k³ 343 Factorised 3k 21 That is roughly a 94% reduction, and — more importantly — it lets the network learn each axis independently, which is exactly what anisotropic data calls for. Putting it together The whole model is a carefully staged U-shaped pipeline: Encoder — 3D Res2Net peels the volume layer by layer, detail to outline. Bottleneck — GCM injects global understanding at the narrowest point. Decoder — at each upsampling step, AFFM fuses intelligently and MACM refines for anisotropy. Output — a final convolution produces a per-voxel probability map. What I took from the structure: each module is a direct answer to a named failure, not a general-purpose improvement. That is what makes the paper easy to follow and hard to argue with.

title.zh: MM-UNet 3D Res2Net 编码器详解：2D 权重扩展与多尺度特征提取
title.en: MM-UNet 3D Res2Net Encoder: Expanding 2D Weights for Multi-Scale Feature Extraction

description.zh: 编码器细节：为什么选 Res2Net、2D 权重怎样改造成 3D，以及通道数增长背后的取舍。
description.en: How 2D pretrained weights become a 3D encoder, and why channel count grows as spatial resolution falls.

text.zh: 阅读约 5 分钟 专题：MM-UNet 论文精读。前置知识：DenseNet、参数量计算、U-Net 结构详解。相关章节：整体架构、AFFM。 编码器细节：3D Res2Net的改造和使用 核心思想 我们选用了一个叫Res2Net的”高手”来做编码器，但它本来是处理2D普通照片的。我们通过一些巧妙的”改造”，让它能处理我们的3D医学图像，并且还让它继承了之前在普通照片上学到的”经验”。 为什么选择Res2Net？ Res2Net的每个残差块内部都有分层式的残差连接，这让它能更有效地在粒度级别使用多尺度信息，扩展每一层的感受野。 就像工人同时拿着多种不同倍数的放大镜在工作： 一个小放大镜看细微的纹理和边缘（小尺度特征） 一个中倍放大镜看局部的结构（中尺度特征） 一个大倍放大镜看大致的轮廓（大尺度特征） 这对于边界模糊的前列腺图像来说，非常有用。 编码器的具体工作流程 第一步：初始卷积（Convolution Stem） 给定的图像首先通过一个卷积茎，它由并行的3×3×3卷积和1×1×1卷积组成，后面跟着求和操作。 3×3×3卷积：捕捉图像中小范围的、基本的局部特征（比如某个点是不是边缘） 1×1×1卷积：主要负责调整数据的通道数，为后续处理做准备 最后把两个结果相加，得到一个包含丰富基础信息的特征图 第二步：核心特征提取 然后依次进入四个Res2Net残差块，生成具有不同空间分辨率的特征。 预备层的输出会依次通过4个串联的Res2Net模块。每经过一个模块，特征图的空间尺寸会变小（下采样），但抽象程度和通道数会增加。这样，我们就得到了4个不同尺度的特征图，它们分别包含了从”细致”到”概括”的信息，为后续解码和融合做准备。 最关键的部分：如何从2D改造到3D？ 改造方法一：第一个层 我们首先将第一层中的7×7 2D卷积替换为7×7×3 3D卷积 具体来说，具有单通道3D输入的7×7×3核等效于Res2Net中具有三通道2D输入的7×7核 改造方法二：其他层 在其他层中，x×x的2D卷积直接转换为x×x×1的3D卷积 为什么要用”预训练”模型？ 我们的编码器可以使用预训练的Res2Net进行初始化…这种初始化可以帮助迁移在大规模自然图像数据集上获得的图像表示能力。 “预训练”就是这个Res2Net”高手”已经在一个包含上百万张普通照片（ImageNet数据集）的”大型综合学校”里毕业了，学会了如何识别各种物体的基本特征（如边缘、形状、纹理）。 好处：我们不做”从零开始”的训练，而是让网络带着这些”基础知识”来学习我们的前列腺MR图像。这就像让一个已经学会”看图”的学生去专门学”看医学影像”，他会上手更快，效果更好。 Res2Net通道数增长机制 通道是什么？ 在卷积神经网络中，一个”通道”可以理解为模型学习到的一种”特征探测器”或一种”专业的描述角度”。 在输入层，对于灰度医学图像，只有1个通道，它代表原始像素的亮度 在网络深层，一个通道可能专门负责探测边缘，另一个通道专门负责探测特定纹理，第三个通道可能专门识别圆弧状结构（可能是前列腺的轮廓） 通道数增加，就意味着模型有了更多”专业的描述角度”来理解和表示图像。 为什么需要增加通道数？ 这背后是”用信息的广度（通道数），来弥补信息的深度（空间尺寸）的损失”的权衡策略。 典型的编码器下采样过程： 层级 空间尺寸（示例） 通道数（示例） 发生了什么？ 输入 128 x 128 x 128 1 原始3D图像，只有亮度信息 第1层后 64 x 64 x 64 64 下采样，空间细节丢失了。但我们生成了64种不同的”基础特征”来描述这个更小的图 第2层后 32 x 32 x 32 128 尺寸再缩小一半。为了不丢失太多信息，我们将通道数翻倍 第3层后 16 x 16 x 16 256 尺寸再次减半。我们继续增加通道数到256 第4层后 8 x 8 x 8 512 到达最底层。空间信息最少，但此时我们有512个高度抽象和专业的”概念”
